title: Take a Look Inside the GR GT’s Aluminum Chassis—a Toyota First
summary: With no Toyota emblems anywhere to be found, the GR GT is the first car by the automaker to be marketed solely under the Gazoo Racing brand. body_text: With no Toyota emblems anywhere to be found, the GR GT is the first car by the automaker to be marketed solely under the Gazoo Racing brand. That’s not the only groundbreaking step for the car; perhaps most notable is its extensive use of aluminum in the chassis. Toyota gave spectators at the Rolex Monterey Motorsports Reunion an up-close look at the aluminum castings that make up the bulk of the chassis of the GR GT and its racing sibling, the GR GT3. They also gave us a peek at the drivetrain. The chassis, which uses nine large aluminum castings that are welded to aluminum tubing and extrusions, is a first for any Toyota product. The castings are an extension of Toyota’s engine casting expertise. Takashi Doi, the Project General Manager of the GR GT and GR GT3, told us that the low-pressure casting requires incredible precision, as the aluminum must flow through narrow passages in the molds around the cured sand cores. The GR GT uses nine major chassis castings. The three that make up the engine crossmemeber and front suspension mounts have already been joined here. Brandan Gillogly The castings are machined where aluminum beams and extrusions will be welded to complete the structure. Brandan Gillogly The GR GT represents a major shift in thinking compared to the company’s last halo car, the Lexus LFA. Where the LFA was beautiful and artistic, crafted to evoke emotion with its Yamaha-tuned V-10 soundtrack, the GR GT is meant to be first and foremost a functional track car. The overall shape is less sculpture and more sledgehammer. We have to say, however, that its form-follows-function look has its own elegance. Brandan Gillogly Toyota is aware that the LFA is loved by enthusiasts for its looks, performance, sound, technology, and engineering. However, its beautifully woven carbon-fiber structure is also a liability. How many LFA owners want to take a risk on track, knowing that skipping off the wall could easily result in a complete loss because there is no way to repair that carbon-fiber structure? In contrast, Toyota is currently developing procedures to ensure that the GR GT’s chassis is repairable. It expects these cars to be driven hard. There are still a lot of questions about the GR GT, and Toyota is keeping plenty of secrets. For example, the total output of the twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 has not yet been announced, although it is promised to be at least 641 hp and 627 lb-ft of torque. There’s also no word on exactly how many of the limited production run will be allocated to North America. So far, the number being discussed is 200-250 units. Andrew Gilleland, Senior Vice President of Toyota Motor North America’s Automotive Operations Group, said he will speak with each of those potential 200-250 buyers personally to get the GR GT into the hands of enthusiasts who will use it as intended. If you might be one of them, it’s probably time to brush up on your track driving skills. In the meantime, have a look at some of the technical details that Toyota was willing to divulge in the photos of the chassis and components below. We also had the opportunity to take a look at a cutaway of the GR GT’s rear-mounted eight-speed automatic transaxle. The transmission sits behind the centerline of the rear wheels, and bevel-cut gears transmit torque forward to the limited-slip differential, allowing the GR GT to keep a compact wheelbase. Brandan Gillogly Rather than a traditional dual clutch, the GR GT uses a clutched hybrid motor. The small chain-driven component is a pump for transmission fluid. Brandan Gillogly The differential has a separate pump driven off a gear attached to the ring gear side of the differential. It’s the only straight-cut gear in the car, and its position, just aft of the driver, provides some racy mechanical noise. Brandan Gillogly Brandan Gillogly Brandan Gillogly One of the main aims of the whole GR GT project was to get the center of gravity as low as possible. The 4.0-liter V-8’s dry-sump oiling system allows it to nestle low into the chassis. Its tank is mounted on the right-hand side, outboard and slightly rearward of the engine. body_text: View all press releases Six Flags Entertainment Corporation Reports 2026 Second Quarter Results August 06, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Strong second quarter results with higher attendance at the Company's current operating portfolio Active pass base up at the Company's current operating portfolio reflecting strong season pass sales and expanded membership offerings, providing greater visibility into peak season demand More focused park portfolio consolidates management efforts and resources to maximize returns at the high-potential parks CHARLOTTE, N.C.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Six Flags Entertainment Corporation (NYSE: FUN) (the “Company” or “Six Flags”) the largest regional amusement park operator in North America, today announced results for its 2026 second quarter ended June 28, 2026. Second Quarter 2026 Results Please note : 2025 second quarter results include quarterly financial and other data related to eight parks Six Flags no longer operated in the 2026 second quarter including: (1) seven parks Six Flags sold to EPR Properties prior to the start of 2026 park operations, and (2) a combined amusement/water park located in Bowie, Maryland, where park operations were discontinued following the end of its 2025 operating season. Therefore, results are presented both on a Reported Basis and on a Same-Park Basis, or excluding the results of the parks sold and closed. As compared with the second quarter of 2025 on a Same-Park Basis: Net revenues totaled $864 million, an increase of $20 million, or 2.4%, from $844 million. Net loss attributable to Six Flags Entertainment Corporation was $194 million, compared with a net loss of $87 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $249 million, an increase of $16 million, or 7%, from $233 million. Attendance totaled 13.1 million visits, an increase of 4%, from 12.7 million visits. Per capita spending was $62.88, a decrease of 1%, from $63.38. Operating days totaled 1,615, a decrease of 44 days, from 1,659. CEO Commentary “Our second quarter and first-half results reflect meaningful progress advancing the strategic priorities we established at the beginning of the year to strengthen the business,” said John Reilly, Six Flags President and CEO. “Our more focused operating portfolio generated higher attendance, net revenues and Adjusted EBITDA, demonstrating that our portfolio actions and performance improvement initiatives are delivering improved financial results. Additionally, season pass and membership sales increased and our active pass base expanded during the second quarter, reinforcing our conviction that we are taking the right steps to build a stronger, more predictable business as we enter the most important part of our operating season. “Our commercial strategy - designed to build a larger, more engaged guest community and create greater long-term value from each guest relationship, demonstrated its effectiveness by delivering tangible results in the second quarter,” Reilly continued. “Guests continue to respond favorably to our flexible, benefit-rich season pass and membership offerings, with season-to-date pass sales increasing 7% and our active pass base growing 6% on a Same-Park Basis. We are also seeing encouraging demand for higher-tier passes and our expanded membership offerings, reflecting the value guests place on greater access and flexibility. Together, these initiatives strengthen recurring revenue, enhance visibility into future demand, and support stronger attendance and financial performance over time. “We are strengthening park-level accountability, sharpening commercial execution, and maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation,” Reilly added. “With the divestiture of seven non-core parks complete, we are focusing our resources on parks with the highest returns. These actions are building a stronger operating company with greater long-term earnings potential. While important work remains, the second quarter results and leading indicators give us increasing confidence in the operating priorities we have established.” Summarized Second Quarter 2026 Results Unless otherwise noted, the discussion below compares the performance of the Company's current operating portfolio, which excludes the results of the parks sold and closed. Same-Park Basis comparisons are presented as supplemental information. Management believes Same-Park Basis information is meaningful to help evaluate operating performance related only to the portfolio of parks that were owned and operated by Six Flags during the comparable periods and uses it for this purpose. Net revenues. On a Reported Basis, the Company's parks generated net revenues of $865 million, a decrease of $65 million, or 7%, compared with $930 million in the second quarter of 2025. On a Same-Park Basis, the Company’s parks generated net revenues of $864 million, an increase of $20 million, or 2.4%, compared with $844 million in the second quarter of 2025. The increase in Same-Park Basis net revenues was driven primarily by 4% higher attendance, including a 10% increase in season-pass visitation, and continued strength in food and extra-charge spending per visit. These benefits were partially offset by lower admissions per capita spending(2), an earlier spring break season falling in this year's first quarter versus last year's second quarter, and approximately 3% fewer operating days. Attendance and operating days . Attendance on a Reported Basis decreased 1.1 million visits, or 7%, compared with the second quarter of 2025. Attendance on a Same-Park Basis increased 449,000 visits, or 4%, compared with the second quarter of 2025. Attendance growth on a Same-Park Basis was supported primarily by increased season pass visitation, reflecting continued strength in the Company's season pass and membership programs across the portfolio. Operating days for the current operating portfolio totaled 1,615, compared with 1,659 operating days for the same parks in the prior-year period. Per capita spending . Per capita spending on a Reported Basis was $62.89, an increase of $0.43, or 1%, compared with $62.46 in the prior-year period. Per capita spending on a Same-Park Basis was $62.88, a decline of $0.50, or 1%, compared with $63.38 in the prior-year period. The modest decline in per capita spending on a Same-Park Basis primarily reflected lower admissions per capita spending associated with expanded season pass benefits and increased cross-park visitation, partially offset by continued strength in guest spending on food, extra-charge attractions and other in-park offerings. Paid admission pricing remained stable year over year, while guests continued to trade up to higher-tier season pass products that provide greater access and flexibility. Management believes its initiatives support higher attendance and increased long-term earnings potential despite modest pressure on admissions per capita spending. Operating costs and expenses . Operating costs and expenses remained well controlled despite higher attendance and guest activity during the quarter. On a Reported Basis, operating expenses decreased $61 million, and selling, general and administrative expense increased $1 million. On a Same-Park Basis, operating expenses increased by only $1 million compared with the prior-year period, as higher maintenance activity, as well as smaller increases in credit card fees, live entertainment costs and utility expenses, were largely offset by lower full-time wage expense and related benefits. Selling, general and administrative expense on a Same-Park Basis also remained well controlled, increasing only $3 million while continuing to support the Company's commercial initiatives and operating priorities. Selling, general and administrative expense on a Same-Park Basis increased due to full-time wages, which was primarily due to an increase in equity compensation and severance costs, and higher consulting and legal costs, both of which were offset by lower advertising costs. The combination of revenue growth and disciplined expense management resulted in stronger operating leverage, allowing a larger portion of incremental revenues to translate into higher earnings during the quarter. Adjusted EBITDA. The Company’s parks generated Adjusted EBITDA of $243 million in both periods on a Reported Basis. On a Same-Park Basis, the Company's parks generated Adjusted EBITDA of $249 million, an increase of $16 million, or 7%, compared with $233 million in the second quarter of 2025. The improvement demonstrates stronger performance from the current operating portfolio. See the attached table for a reconciliation of net loss to Adjusted EBITDA. Season Pass, Membership and Active Pass Base Progress During the second quarter, the Company continued to build momentum in its season pass and membership programs, supported by a more differentiated product architecture, expanded regional and all-park access available with certain products, improved marketing execution, and a more coordinated approach to guest acquisition and retention. The active pass base increased 6% compared with the same time last year on a Same-Park Basis. Management views the number of guests eligible to visit the parks as an important leading indicator of attendance and a source of greater visibility into demand during the balance of the season. Sales mix continued to shift toward higher-tier pass products, reflecting guest response to the added access and enhanced benefits available with those offerings. The mix improvement supports higher-value guest relationships without relying solely on lower headline pricing. Membership participation continued to expand during the quarter. Member counts beyond their initial 12-month term exceeded the prior-year level at a higher average price, and the Company expanded its membership model to six additional parks in June 2026. Membership provides guests with a lower upfront purchase commitment while building the Company’s recurring-revenue base and supporting continued growth in the active pass base. Marketing investment produced improved acquisition and conversion efficiency during the quarter, supporting growth in pass sales and the active pass base while improving the economic return on guest acquisition spending. The Company also introduced several major thrill rides, attractions and entertainment offerings during the quarter. These investments are designed to strengthen the guest proposition, support visitation and improve the return generated by the Company’s established park base. Balance Sheet and Liquidity Highlights The Company continued to strengthen its balance sheet during the first six months of 2026 through improved operating cash flow, disciplined capital spending, and the use of proceeds from previously announced portfolio transactions to reduce outstanding borrowings. The Company also reduced borrowings under its revolving credit facility and maintained substantial available capacity at quarter-end. Reducing leverage remains an essential financial priority. As of June 28, 2026, the Company reported the following: Total deferred revenue of $431 million. On a Reported Basis, total deferred revenue decreased $30 million. On a Same-Park Basis, total deferred revenue increased $8 million, or 2%, compared with the prior year, supported by growth in membership and advance sales. Cash and cash equivalents of $135 million. Total liquidity of $837 million, including $703 million available under the Company’s revolving credit facility. Net debt (3) totaled $4.9 billion, calculated as total debt of $5.0 billion (before debt issuance costs and acquisition fair value layers) less cash and cash equivalents of $135 million. Conference Call As previously announced, Six Flags Entertainment Corporation will host a conference call with analysts starting at 8 a.m. ET today, August 6, 2026, to discuss its recent financial results. Participants on the call will include Six Flags CEO John Reilly and CFO Ash Walia. Investors and all other interested parties can access a live, listen-only audio webcast of the call on the Six Flags Investors website at https://investors.sixflags.com under the tabs Investor Information / Events & Presentations. Those unable to listen to the live webcast can access a recorded version of the call on the Six Flags Investors website at https://investors.sixflags.com under Investor Information / Events and Presentations, shortly after the live call’s completion. A digital recording of the conference call will be available for replay by phone starting at approximately 1 p.m. ET on Thursday August 6, 2026, until 11:59 p.m. ET on Thursday August 13, 2026. To access the phone replay in North America please dial (800) 770-2030; from international locations please dial +1 (609) 800-9909, followed by Conference ID 3720518. About Six Flags Entertainment Corporation Six Flags Entertainment Corporation (NYSE: FUN) is North America’s largest regional amusement-resort operator, with 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resort properties across 13 states in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico. The Company also manages an amusement park in Saudi Arabia. Focused on its purpose of creating FUN, thrills and a lifetime of memories, Six Flags provides immersive entertainment to millions of guests every year with world-class coasters, themed rides, thrilling water parks, resorts and a portfolio of beloved intellectual property such as Looney Tunes®, DC Comics® and PEANUTS®. title: Maiwald Chooses Solve Intelligence for Selected AI-Supported IP Workflows
summary: Solve Intelligence is proud to share that Maiwald, one of Germany’s largest and most progressive intellectual property firms, works with Solve Intelligence on selected AI-supported workflows in its patent and legal practice groups. Following an evaluation period during which selected functionalities were assessed for approved internal use cases, Maiwald and Solve have formed an enterprise partnership for 2026.
body_text: Key Insights Maiwald explored Solve’s functionalities during a fixed evaluation period culminating in an enterprise partnership after evaluating multiple solutions on the market. Charts gives Maiwald’s litigation team one source-cited environment, e.g., for invalidity charts, claim construction, and evaluation of search results: the groundwork behind opposition, nullity, infringement and UPC matters. The platform’s depth in life sciences also including ChemDraw®1 as embedded chemical drawing editor facilitates patent work across biologics and small molecules, one of the firm’s most important practice areas. The partnership is supported on the ground by Solve’s Munich office and a dedicated, German-speaking team admitted before the UPC, the German courts and the EPO, with private-practice experience across the firm’s core fields, including life sciences. About Maiwald Maiwald is one of Germany’s largest and best-known IP firms, with more than 280 staff members across its offices in Munich and Düsseldorf. Its interdisciplinary teams, comprising more than 110 patent attorneys, attorneys-at-law and technical specialists including an in-house patent search department, advise clients of every size and sector, in Germany, Europe and beyond. The firm’s technical breadth is exceptional, running from pharmaceuticals, biotechnology and chemistry, which have long been a particular strength, through to electrical and mechanical engineering, communications and IT, mobility and energy, and medical technology. Maiwald’s work spans the full patent lifecycle, from drafting and worldwide prosecution to FTO opinions and complex portfolio management, alongside a leading contentious practice: opposition and appeal before the German and European Patent Offices, infringement and nullity before the national courts, and representation before the Unified Patent Court, with attorneys-at-law experienced in coordinating cross-border litigation. The firm is consistently ranked by IAM Patent 1000, MIP IP Stars, Chambers, JUVE Patent and The Legal 500. They are also voted one of the best commercial law firms by brandeins and Statista. The bar at Maiwald is high. A technically demanding docket, complex multi-jurisdictional disputes, and a quality standard maintained for decades meant that any AI platform had to prove it could meet the firm where it works. Evaluation Period Maiwald conducted an evaluation period during which various functionalities were assessed for selected internal use cases. The key to a successful evaluation and implementation requires the level of organisation and teamwork that Maiwald is known for and a solution that enhances the commercial judgement of its attorneys as they look to achieve the best outcome for their clients in every case. "With its intuitive usability and transparent prompting, Solve Intelligence makes the use of AI in the patent field easily accessible. The platform helps us evaluate large volumes of information efficiently and creates more room for what we do best: providing strategic advice to our clients." - Dr. Regina Neuefeind, Partner at Maiwald Solve Intelligence in Action Maiwald’s attorneys are now evaluating and using Solve Intelligence in selected use cases. Prosecution, opposition and appeal . The platform summarises examiner objections, identifies the key grounds of rejection, and surfaces counterarguments and prosecution avenues for attorney review across EPO and German Patent Office practice, and into opposition and appeal, while the substantive decisions stay with the attorney. Charts, built for the litigation team . Charts is where Solve supports the firm’s contentious practice. In one source-cited, auditable environment, Maiwald’s litigators and patent attorneys generate and analyse invalidity claim charts for nullity actions and EPO oppositions, conduct claim construction analyses, and evaluate search results. Depth in life sciences . Life sciences and chemistry are among Maiwald’s defining strengths, and the platform is built for that type of work. Practitioners can create ChemDraw® structures and import and validate ST.26 sequence listings. Across dense prior-art domains like biologics, small molecules and diagnostics, the platform also gives claim-level visibility for portfolio reviews: mapping coverage against therapeutic areas, biosimilar entrants and competitor filings, and exposure across patent term and regulatory exclusivity. Solve Assistant . Solve’s agentic Assistant, the newest module, is already in use, handling everyday, multi-step tasks from searching portfolios, drafting letters, and legal research. Supported from Solve’s Munich Office This is a partnership with people behind it, not just a licence to software. Maiwald is supported on the ground by Solve’s Munich office and by a dedicated, German-speaking team matched to the firm’s practice areas: patent litigators and patent attorneys admitted before the Unified Patent Court, the German courts and the European Patent Office, with years of private-practice experience across the firm’s core fields, including life sciences. Around 35% of Solve’s team are qualified patent attorneys and IP specialists, so Maiwald’s attorneys work with people who understand the craft and the forums they practise in. That same team leads the rollout, building custom AI styles and templates by team, client and jurisdiction, and Solve looks forward to continuing the partnership in person in Germany. “This is a collaborative partnership. We are pleased to support Maiwald in selected AI-supported workflows for IP work , and Solve will continue to build the go-to AI platform for German and global patent practice.” - Dr. Lukas Wollenschlaeger from Solve Intelligence’s Munich office, previously a patent litigator at Hogan Lovells Technology That Keeps the Attorney in Control Maiwald’s adoption of Solve isn’t about replacing what makes the firm exceptional. Its attorneys bring deep scientific training, decades of prosecution and litigation experience, and a record of securing and defending consequential patents. What Solve does is take the mechanical work off their plate, so they can focus where their expertise decides outcomes: prosecution and opposition strategy, the analysis behind a dispute, portfolio positioning, and multi-jurisdictional filing and litigation across the EPO, the national courts and the UPC. For a firm that has spent decades defining excellent IP practice in Europe, that is exactly the right use of AI. ‍ 1 ChemDraw® is a registered trade mark of Revvity Signals Software, Inc. ‍

title: Kevin Jones named President of Deluxe Merchant Services
summary: Founder of recently acquired Celero Commerce brings 20-plus years of experience to Deluxe MINNEAPOLIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Deluxe (NYSE: DLX), a…...
body_text: Kevin Jones named President of Deluxe Merchant Services August 17, 2026 4:30 pm EDT Download as PDF Founder of recently acquired Celero Commerce brings 20-plus years of experience to Deluxe MINNEAPOLIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Deluxe (NYSE: DLX), a trusted payments and data company, today announced the appointment of Kevin Jones as President of its Merchant Services division. Jones founded Celero Commerce in 2018, rapidly scaling it to process more than $28 billion across 175 banking partners and 55,000 small business customers annually. Deluxe acquired Celero earlier this month, positioning Deluxe Merchant Services as a top-10 non-bank merchant acquirer, based on Nilson reporting. Prior to launching Celero, Jones led First American Payment Systems’ strategic partner channel before leaving to found Anovia Payments, where he delivered an 8.5x investment return. Deluxe later acquired First American in 2021, which now serves as the backbone of the company’s Merchant Services division. “Kevin brings the experience and leadership to expand our merchant business, and I am excited to welcome him as part of the Deluxe leadership team,” said Barry McCarthy, President and CEO of Deluxe. “He brings the perspective that comes with creating entirely new ventures in a rapidly changing payments environment and has helped the payments industry evolve in ways we could’ve only imagined 10 years ago. His demonstrated ability to deliver for customers and drive ROI is a natural fit for our culture.” Jones’ track record has been one of implementing innovative payments solutions through a user-friendly high-tech bundle. “I am excited to be joining Barry and the team at Deluxe,” Jones said. “The strength, scale, and scope of the combined entity position us to win and grow faster than either organization could alone. The marriage of shared customer focus, distribution channels, proprietary processing platforms, and award-winning service creates a uniquely compelling offer in the marketplace.” About Deluxe Corporation Deluxe, a trusted payments and data company, champions business so communities thrive. Our solutions help businesses pay, get paid, and grow. For more than 100 years, Deluxe customers have relied on our solutions and platforms at all stages of their lifecycle, from start-up to maturity. Our powerful scale supports millions of small businesses, thousands of vital financial institutions and hundreds of the world’s largest consumer brands, while processing more than $2 trillion in annual payment volume. Our reach, scale and distribution channels position Deluxe to be our customers’ most trusted business partner. To learn how we can help your business, visit us at www.deluxe.com . title: Inside Humboldt Family Farms: How One California Collective Is Shifting Consumers to Craft Sungrown Cannabis
summary: Humboldt Family Farms is building the infrastructure that enables independent Humboldt County growers to reach California dispensary shelves under their own names.
body_text: Humboldt County may be one of the most recognizable cannabis-growing regions. But for decades, many of the small farmers responsible for that reputation have struggled to capture the value of the name they helped build. Humboldt Family Farms is trying to change that—and there is growing evidence that retailers and consumers are responding. Today, Humboldt Family Farms has built a growing retail presence across California, connecting independent Humboldt farms to consumers through packaging, sales, marketing, distribution, cultural integrations and retail support. Humboldt Family Farms is proving what can happen when sungrown cannabis is treated as a category worth explaining rather than simply a lower-priced alternative to indoor flower. During a campaign with Embarc and SURFER Magazine, sungrown flower and pre-rolls grew from 4% of sales in June to 12% in August across Embarc stores. That result speaks to something bigger than a single successful campaign. The problem may not be that California consumers don't want sungrown cannabis. The problem may be that much of the industry has not given them a reason to understand it. Building a Category, Not Just Selling Flower Walk into a California dispensary and cannabis is still largely presented through potency, price, strain name, package design, and whether the flower was grown indoor or outdoor. That leaves an enormous amount of information out of the conversation. Where was it grown? Who grew it? How long has that family been farming? What genetics are being preserved? How was the land treated? What does the purchase actually support? Those questions are familiar in wine, coffee, food, and other agricultural categories. Humboldt Family Farms believes cannabis should be no different. Its partner farms cultivate under natural sunlight, operate at relatively small scales, and include growers who use regenerative agriculture, native soils, closed-loop composting, beneficial insects, dry-farming techniques, and other practices developed over years of working the same land. The collective also works with genetics that don't necessarily follow whatever's trending on the menu that month. Maui Waui. Blue Dream. Train Wreck. Galaxy OG. Sapphire Tsu. Wildberry Pie. Salted Caramel. Hawaiian Fanta. Humboldt Family Farms Grapelicious, a top selling strain for the company Some have histories stretching back years on the farms that continue to grow them. For a retailer, this creates another way to merchandise cannabis. Instead of competing exclusively around THC and price, the conversation can include provenance, genetics, farming practices, sustainability, regional identity, and the people responsible for the flower. And when HFF has put those ideas in front of consumers, they have translated into sales. From 4% to 12% In 2025 and 2026, Humboldt Family Farms worked with Embarc and SURFER Magazine on a “surf and sungrown” campaign built around the natural overlap between California surf culture and Humboldt agriculture. The collaboration included Maui Waui flower and pre-rolls, with pre-roll tubes made using reclaimed ocean plastic. It also resulted in the first cannabis advertisement to appear in SURFER Magazine's 65-year history. The cultural connection was easy to understand: independence, outdoor life, California heritage, and respect for the natural environment. But the retail result is what made the campaign especially significant. Across Embarc stores, sungrown flower and pre-rolls increased from 4% of sales in June to 12% in August. Consumers didn't suddenly discover sunlight. The products were given context. That distinction matters for retailers because sungrown has often been merchandised primarily through value. Once price becomes the defining characteristic of a category, it becomes difficult for growers or retailers to build much equity around it. HFF is testing a different proposition: give sungrown an identity, explain why Humboldt matters, introduce customers to the farmers, and connect the product to communities where those values already make sense. SURFER is one example. HFF has also worked with POWDER Magazine and participated in events including the Dead & Company 60th Anniversary, Outside Lands, Cali Roots, and the California State Fair. The objective isn't celebrity adjacency. It's finding places where the people, product, and culture have a legitimate connection. Humboldt's Name Has Value. Most Farmers Never Capture It. This is the problem at the center of Humboldt Family Farms. Humboldt County spent decades becoming synonymous with cannabis, yet much of the cannabis grown there eventually reaches consumers without the identity of the individual farm attached to it. The region creates value. The farmer creates value. But somewhere between cultivation and the retail shelf, much of that identity can disappear. HFF founder Scott Vasterling saw an opportunity to build infrastructure around the farms without absorbing them. The idea was straightforward: “To provide small craft family farmers a platform to get them to retail with efficiency and scale.” Instead of asking every small farmer to independently build a sales organization, marketing department, packaging operation, testing program, distribution network, and statewide retail relationships, HFF provides those functions collectively. The farmers remain farmers. They stay independent. They stay on their land. And importantly, their identities don't have to disappear when their cannabis leaves Humboldt. For retailers, that means the name on the package can lead somewhere real. The Farms Behind the Flower Full Moon Farms Nik Erickson has farmed in Humboldt County since 1993. Today he operates three grow sites along Highway 36 near Mad River, with each property influenced by its own elevation, weather, and microclimate. Rows of trellised sungrown cannabis plants growing on Full Moon Farms, backlit by afternoon sun. Vasterling describes him simply: “Nik represents the true Humboldt farmer: family-run, sungrown, and craft-first.” In spring 2025, an ATV accident tore through Erickson's hip just as the cultivation season was beginning. His partner, Darien, and the farm crew kept the operation moving while he recovered. By midsummer, Erickson was back on his feet. Today, Full Moon flower reaches dispensary shelves throughout California through Humboldt Family Farms, without requiring Full Moon to give up the identity it spent decades building. As Erickson puts it: “You get to stay on your land and keep your name. That's the whole point.” Neukom Family Farm Jacques Neukom began farming along the Trinity River near Willow Creek in 1996 with an 81-tree orchard. Amy Neukom (foreground) and Scott Vasterling (background) on the Neukom Family Farm in Willow Creek Today, Jacques and Amy Neukom manage more than 1,600 fruit trees, including 18 varieties of peaches and 15 types of pluots. Their cannabis operation? Approximately 5,000 square feet. “We want it to be a part of our farm,” Amy said, “but not our entire reality.” That distinction says a lot about what small-scale Humboldt agriculture actually looks like. Neukom Family Farm is Sun+Earth Certified and CCOF Certified Organic. The family works with native no-till soil, closed-loop composting, dry-farming practices, and beneficial insects rather than relying on conventional chemical inputs. Its Sapphire Tsu has also become the foundation for one of HFF's collaborative pre-roll offerings. The Neukoms have watched the perception of their livelihood change around them. Years ago, some local families kept their distance because the Neukoms grew cannabis. By the time their daughter graduated, some of those same parents were telling their children that if they were going to smoke cannabis, they should smoke flower grown by the Neukoms. That isn't a marketing campaign. It's what happens when people know who grows their cannabis. What HFF Gives Retailers That relationship between farm and consumer is difficult to recreate once cannabis becomes anonymous. It is also where Humboldt Family Farms believes it can offer retailers something useful. HFF gives buyers access to independent Humboldt farms through a single platform, rather than requiring them to build individual relationships with dozens of small cultivators. That platform brings together recognizable Humboldt origin, documented farm histories, regenerative and certified cultivation partners, distinctive genetics, statewide distribution, retail education, marketing support, and cultural collaborations. The result isn't simply another collection of SKUs. A retailer can use HFF to build out a sungrown category, introduce customers to Humboldt agriculture, train staff on cultivation and provenance, support sustainability initiatives, and offer products in which the farmer's identity remains part of what is being sold. The 4% to 12% growth at Embarc suggests there is commercial potential when those pieces work together. Why This Matters Now The timing is important because the small-farm community that built Humboldt's cannabis reputation has been shrinking. Planting cannabis on Full Moon Farms Legalization didn't simply open a door to a larger market. It brought regulatory expenses, compliance requirements, taxation, volatile wholesale pricing, and a retail system that can be extraordinarily difficult for small independent cultivators to access. Scale tends to solve those problems. But scale can also erase exactly what made Humboldt valuable in the first place. HFF's answer has been to scale the infrastructure rather than the farms. Packaging can scale. Distribution can scale. Sales can scale. Marketing can scale. The individual farm doesn't necessarily have to. That distinction allows a farmer like Nik Erickson or the Neukom family to remain relatively small while participating in a statewide market that increasingly rewards size and operational efficiency. It also gives retailers a direct way to support those farms without sacrificing the logistical simplicity required to run a modern cannabis business. How Humboldt Family Farms Got Here Humboldt Family Farms didn't begin as an attempt to manufacture a new identity for Humboldt cannabis. The identity already existed. The challenge was figuring out how to preserve it through legalization. Vasterling's experience before entering cannabis included time around brands such as Guayakí, Patagonia, and The North Face—companies that demonstrated how provenance, values, community, and product can reinforce one another when the connection is legitimate. After moving to Humboldt and becoming part of a cannabis-farming family, he encountered a very different business reality. Small farms could grow exceptional cannabis yet lack the resources to package, market, distribute, build retailer relationships, and compete with substantially larger operators. Humboldt Family Farms developed around that gap. Over time, the collective expanded its farm network, retail presence, product portfolio, distribution capabilities, and cultural partnerships while keeping the original premise intact: the platform should serve the farms rather than replace them. What Comes Next Following the 2026 California State Fair, Humboldt Family Farms is continuing to expand its presence throughout California. That includes deeper retail partnerships, broader access to its sungrown portfolio, and additional collaborations across art, music, food, outdoor culture, and other communities where Humboldt's agricultural identity has relevance. But expansion creates its own test. The opportunity isn't simply to put Humboldt Family Farms into more dispensaries. It's to prove that California can build a meaningful craft sungrown category—and that the farmers who gave Humboldt its name can participate in the economic value of that category. For decades, Humboldt farmers helped make the county famous. The next chapter is making sure consumers know who they are. ‍ Shop Humboldt Family Farms on Nabis Marketplace. ‍

title: Eva Defense Signs Development Agreement with Boumarang to Develop Jam-Resistant Communications Drone
summary: Program targets a sub-55-pound unmanned aircraft system designed to keep operating where GPS and radio links are degraded or denied. Following the formation of Eva Defense, the addition of senior military leadership, and previously announced letters of intent, Eva Live continues building a next-generation defense technology platform focused on autonomous systems, resilient communications, and AI. […]
body_text: Program targets a sub-55-pound unmanned aircraft system designed to keep operating where GPS and radio links are degraded or denied. Following the formation of Eva Defense, the addition of senior military leadership, and previously announced letters of intent, Eva Live continues building a next-generation defense technology platform focused on autonomous systems, resilient communications, and AI. LAS VEGAS, NV, Aug. 6, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Eva Live Inc. (NASDAQ: GOAI) (“Eva Live” or the “Company”), an artificial intelligence-driven technology company, today announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Eva Defense Inc. (“Eva Defense”), has entered into a development agreement with Boumarang Inc. (“Boumarang”) to develop a resilient communications unmanned aircraft system (“UAS”). Under the agreement, Eva Defense will fund a twelve-month development program under which Boumarang will design, build, and test the platform. The Company has committed $1.2 million, payable at $100,000 per month from August 5, 2026 through July 31, 2027. Program Highlights • Aircraft class: Sub-55-pound unmanned aircraft system, intended for tactical deployment. • Problem addressed: Maintaining command, control, and data links in DDIL (Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, and Limited) conditions — when satellite navigation and GPS/PNT are degraded or denied and radio-frequency (RF) communications are jammed, intermittent, or bandwidth-constrained. • Structure: Twelve-month program organized around staged technical gates – feasibility, proof of concept, field test, and beta gate – with Eva Defense approval required to proceed at each. • Targeted outcome: 10 to 20 field-tested, beta-ready prototypes, a low-rate initial production plan, and an NDAA-compliant supplier base. The agreement represents the latest step in Eva Live’s broader strategy to establish Eva Defense as a developer of advanced autonomous defense technologies. Over recent months, the Company has assembled experienced military leadership, expanded its defense initiatives, and announced letters of intent for proposed acquisitions intended to accelerate its entry into one of the world’s fastest-growing technology sectors. The program is intended to produce a sub-55-pound resilient communications drone platform designed for operation in contested, communications-denied DDIL environments — in plain terms, a DDIL-capable, jam-resistant small drone built to keep flying its mission and keep transmitting when command-and-control links, GPS, cloud access, or data transmission are jammed, disrupted, unreliable, or bandwidth-constrained. The program will follow a structured, milestone-driven development process progressing from architecture and prototype development through field testing and commercialization readiness. The platform is intended to support secure communications, autonomous mission execution, resilient networking, and future integration with intelligent fleet-management capabilities for government and allied customers. “Defense technology is no longer a future opportunity, it is one of the fastest-growing sectors in the global technology economy,” said David Boulette, Chief Executive Officer of Eva Live. “Over the past several months we have been deliberately building Eva Defense into a company capable of serving this market. We’ve assembled experienced leadership, expanded our strategic relationships, and are now executing on the technology itself. This agreement with Boumarang is a defined engineering program with measurable milestones.” Boumarang, incorporated in Delaware in 2024, develops hydrogen-powered, AI-enabled unmanned air and maritime systems from corporate offices in Irvine, California, and engineering facilities in Austin, Texas. Boumarang was selected for its expertise in autonomous aircraft engineering, RF communications, prototype manufacturing, systems integration, and fleet telemetry. The partnership allows Eva Defense to accelerate development while leveraging these engineering capabilities within a disciplined product-development framework. The Company believes resilient communications will become one of the defining technologies of next-generation autonomous military systems as governments increasingly prioritize DDIL-capable, jam-resistant drones able to maintain operational effectiveness in GPS-degraded and communications-contested environments. Industry estimates from MarketsandMarkets and Grand View Research project the defense drone market to exceed $20 billion by 2030 , driven by increasing defense spending, AI-enabled autonomy, and rapidly evolving battlefield requirements. At the same time, governments worldwide continue to increase investment in autonomous platforms, resilient communications, electronic warfare capabilities, and next-generation defense technologies. Eva Live has not generated revenue from the defense market to date, and there can be no assurance that the Company will capture any portion of this market. Rather than pursuing individual products, Eva Defense is executing a broader strategy to build an integrated defense technology platform focused on autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, resilient communications, and mission-critical software designed for government and allied customers. Craig Nehrkorn, Chief Executive Officer of Boumarang, added: “We’re excited to work alongside Eva Defense as it rapidly expands its defense technology platform. By combining Boumarang’s expertise in autonomous systems, RF engineering, and rapid product development with Eva Defense’s strategic vision, we believe we can accelerate development of a resilient communications platform designed for the next generation of government and allied missions.” The development effort will include product architecture, communications systems integration, mission-planning software, prototype manufacturing, laboratory validation, field testing, and progression toward low-rate initial production readiness, subject to development milestones and future business decisions. The program is at an early development stage. It has no customer, contract award, or program of record. Management believes this agreement further advances Eva Defense’s strategy of becoming a diversified developer of advanced autonomous defense technologies while creating additional long-term opportunities for strategic partnerships, government engagement, and future commercialization. Deliverables under the agreement are assigned to Eva Defense upon payment in full for the applicable deliverable. Boumarang retains its background technology, which is licensed to Eva Defense on a non-exclusive basis to the extent incorporated in those deliverables. About Eva Defense Inc. Eva Defense Inc. is a wholly owned subsidiary of Eva Live Inc. focused on developing artificial intelligence technologies for defense, autonomous systems, unmanned platforms, and advanced command-and-control applications. Its integrated platform — the GOAT aircraft, SwarmOS, and mmWave Link — is designed to improve situational awareness, autonomous coordination, mission planning, and operational effectiveness across defense and government applications. title: Migrate from Zendesk to Freshdesk: Step-by-Step Zendesk Migration Guide
summary: Learn how to migrate from Zendesk to Freshdesk with step-by-step guidance, migration tips, pricing, and best practices.
body_text: Most IT and HR teams discover too late that moving from Zendesk to Freshdesk solves the pricing problem but not the adoption problem. Employees may submit requests through Freshdesk's portal, email, or other configured channels, but Slack-first organizations should evaluate how much of the request and resolution experience can remain inside the workspace employees already use. The migration itself is straightforward. Third-party tools can transfer tickets, contacts, and knowledge base articles between platforms. But the real question is whether Freshdesk, or any traditional help desk, actually serves teams that live in Slack. Before investing weeks in data migration and change management, consider whether a Slack-native help desk might eliminate the need for migration entirely by turning channels like #it-help into fully functional service desks. This guide walks through the Zendesk-to-Freshdesk migration process for teams using Freshdesk as an internal ticketing system. Organizations that need formal ITSM capabilities such as structured service requests, change management, and deeper asset workflows should also evaluate Freshservice, Freshworks' dedicated IT service management product. Key Takeaways A successful Zendesk to Freshdesk migration requires systematic auditing of your current setup before transferring any data, including ticket fields, custom objects, macros, automations, SLA policies, and knowledge base articles Data mapping and migration tool selection determine whether the transition preserves historical context or creates fragmented records that hurt the team's ability to serve internal stakeholders Freshdesk paid plans start at $15 per agent per month when billed annually. Zendesk lists Support Team at $19, Suite Team at $55, and Suite Professional at $115 per agent per month when billed annually Traditional help desk migrations often overlook the fundamental question: whether either platform actually fits how modern teams work, particularly those operating primarily in Slack or Microsoft Teams A case study of Lemonade using Unthread shows that it resolved 40% of tickets automatically , eliminating the need for migration entirely by meeting employees where they already work Setup time depends on scope and complexity: one third-party comparison estimates roughly 4-8 weeks for a properly planned Zendesk deployment and 1-2 weeks for Freshdesk. Slack-native platforms can often begin handling requests quickly, but integrations, workflows, permissions, and enterprise rollout requirements affect the full implementation timeline. Understanding Your Current Zendesk Setup Every successful migration starts with understanding exactly what is being moved. Zendesk implementations accumulate years of customizations, automations, and institutional knowledge that silently break when transferred without proper documentation. Inventorying Zendesk Assets for Migration Start by cataloging everything that powers current help desk operations: Ticket fields and custom objects identify the data structure the team relies on for routing, reporting, and resolution tracking Agent roles and permissions define who can access what, and recreating these incorrectly in Freshdesk creates security gaps SLA policies determine response and resolution targets that the team is measured against Macros and automations represent institutional knowledge about common issues and standard responses Knowledge base articles contain documentation that employees actively reference Integration connections link the help desk to HRIS systems, identity providers, and workflow tools Many organizations underestimate the volume of customizations accumulated over time. Zendesk's configuration complexity can extend implementation timelines, with one third-party comparison estimating a 4-8 week deployment for a properly configured environment. Identifying Critical Data and Configurations Not everything needs to migrate. Closed tickets older than 24 months rarely get referenced. Macros built for departed team members or discontinued processes add clutter. The audit phase is the opportunity to clean house. Focus on identifying which configurations actively support current workflows versus which exist as legacy artifacts. This distinction reduces migration scope and prevents importing problems into the new system. Planning Your Freshdesk Migration The data migration process requires clear decisions about scope, timing, and tooling before any actual transfer begins. Defining Migration Scope and Data Mapping Strategy Map every Zendesk field to its Freshdesk equivalent. Freshdesk's native import capabilities are limited to contacts and companies. Tickets and knowledge base content need third-party migration tools. Create explicit decisions for these common migration challenges: Custom field mapping when Freshdesk does not have exact equivalents to Zendesk fields User and organization matching to prevent duplicate records Attachment handling for tickets with large file attachments Tag and category translation between the two systems' different taxonomies Choosing the Right Migration Approach Three primary options exist for transferring data: Native import tools handle basic contact and company data but lack comprehensive ticket migration capabilities. They work for smaller implementations with minimal customization. Third-party migration services like Help Desk Migration specialize in platform-to-platform transfers. These tools maintain relationships between tickets, comments, and attachments that manual exports break. Custom API scripts provide maximum control but require development resources. Unthread's flexible API demonstrates how modern platforms support custom integration work, making it possible to orchestrate complex migrations or maintain connections between multiple systems. The best price-to-feature ratio matters less than choosing migration methods that preserve the context teams need to serve employees effectively. Executing the Data Migration Execution requires careful timing, validation checkpoints, and rollback plans for when transfers do not complete as expected. Leveraging Specialized Migration Tools Third-party migration services offer pre-built connectors that handle the complexity of mapping Zendesk's data model to Freshdesk's structure. Key capabilities to evaluate include: Incremental migration support for transferring data in phases rather than all at once Field mapping interfaces that define how custom fields translate between systems Validation reports showing what transferred successfully versus what failed Rollback capabilities when migrations encounter errors mid-transfer Migration time depends on ticket volume, custom fields, attachments, knowledge base content, testing requirements, and the chosen cutover strategy. Build time into the project for a test migration, validation, corrections, and a final incremental transfer. Implementing a Phased Migration Approach Rather than attempting a single massive transfer, phase the migration: Phase 1: Test migration with sample data validates that mappings work correctly before touching production records. Phase 2: Historical data transfer moves closed tickets and archived content during off-hours when support volume is lowest. Phase 3: Active ticket migration requires careful coordination to prevent responses from falling through cracks during the transition window. Phase 4: Knowledge base and automation migration completes the transfer after agents are operating in the new system. For teams considering whether this effort is worthwhile, note that teams using Freshservice can connect it with Unthread so Slack conversations create Freshservice tickets and selected ticket updates synchronize between the two systems. Teams migrating specifically to Freshdesk should confirm integration requirements and availability before planning a hybrid deployment. Post-Migration Optimization: Configuring Freshdesk for Internal Support With data transferred, optimization begins. Freshdesk requires configuration work to match the service levels the team previously achieved. Fine-Tuning Freshdesk Settings Freshdesk's intuitive interface and faster setup compared to Zendesk helps, but configuration is still required: Automation rules for ticket routing based on category, priority, and assignee availability SLA policies matching the organization's response and resolution commitments Agent productivity settings including canned responses and scenario automations Reporting dashboards that surface the metrics leadership actually reviews Freshdesk offers Freddy AI capabilities through a combination of plan features and paid add-ons. New Growth, Pro, and Enterprise customers receive a one-time allocation of 500 Freddy AI Agent sessions, while additional AI Agent sessions and Freddy AI Copilot are purchased separately. Enhancing Employee Experience For internal support teams serving IT, HR, and operations requests, consider whether Freshdesk's portal-based model actually fits how employees work. Most employees prefer staying in Slack rather than navigating to a separate ticketing portal. Unthread's shared email inbox can turn incoming internal-support emails into trackable requests that teams manage alongside Slack-based tickets. Organizations that want Freshdesk to remain the system of record should verify the available integration path before designing this workflow. Elevating Service with AI and Automations Traditional help desk software treats AI as an add-on feature. Modern platforms build around purpose-built AI agents that understand request intent and take action autonomously. Implementing Advanced AI for Automated Support The gap between basic chatbots and true agentic AI is substantial. Basic automation matches keywords to canned responses. Purpose-built AI agents understand context, reference knowledge bases, and execute multi-step workflows. Lemonade deployed Unthread across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams. Their results demonstrate what is possible: 40% of incoming tickets resolved automatically across all five departments, not just simple access requests. This matters because actual AI resolution rates depend on knowledge quality, request mix, connected systems, workflow design, and how the platform defines a resolved or deflected ticket. In Unthread's Lemonade case study, approximately 40% of incoming tickets were resolved automatically across multiple internal departments. Unthread's agentic AI supports a broad range of internal support use cases: IT requests for software provisioning, hardware issues, and access management HR inquiries about benefits, payroll, parental leave, and policy questions Finance questions regarding expense reports, purchase orders, and budget approvals Legal requests for contract reviews and compliance guidance Procurement needs for vendor setup and purchase requisitions Building Intelligent Workflows Beyond AI responses, workflow automation handles the operational tasks that consume IT and HR team time. Natural language or visual builders create automations without coding: Approval chains that route requests through appropriate managers Account provisioning that triggers when new employees join Escalation paths that notify on-call staff when SLAs approach breach Cross-system updates that sync ticket status to Jira, Linear, or HRIS systems The difference in admin overhead matters. Unthread's configuration is easier for admins to set up initially and easier to adjust later as workflows, routing rules, and automations change. Traditional help desks like Zendesk and Freshdesk require more specialized knowledge to modify. Addressing Zendesk Pricing Concerns Pricing often drives the initial migration decision. Understanding the full cost picture helps teams make better choices. Comparing Zendesk and Freshdesk Pricing Models Zendesk lists Support Team at $19, Suite Team at $55, and Suite Professional at $115 per agent per month when billed annually. The Copilot add-on is $50 per agent per month, and enterprise organizations may also incur usage-based AI Agent charges. Freshdesk offers a Free Program for two users, with paid plans starting at $15 per agent per month when billed annually. Pro tier runs $49-55 per agent with Freddy AI capabilities available through plan features and paid add-ons. For a 10-agent team over one year, the comparison shows: Zendesk Suite Professional with Copilot : approximately $19,800 annually for 10 agents ($115 + $50 per agent per month, billed annually), excluding any usage-based AI Agent charges Freshdesk Pro : approximately $5,880 ($49 × 10 × 12) Unthread Pro : approximately $9,000 ( $75 × 10 × 12 ) Evaluating Modern Alternatives Teams researching alternatives often evaluate whether a portal-first help desk fits employees who already submit internal requests through Slack or Microsoft Teams. Both Zendesk and Freshdesk are primarily structured around their own service workspaces, even though they support multiple intake channels and integrations. Slack-first organizations should evaluate whether employees and internal agents can complete the full request workflow without unnecessary context switching. For Slack-first organizations, this creates friction that drives down adoption. Employees work around the help desk by DMing IT staff directly or posting in random channels, creating the untracked requests that help desks exist to prevent. Unthread's approach turns a specific Slack channel like #it-help into a full internal help desk. The channel becomes a single intake location for employee requests, with some ticket types remaining in-channel while others move to DMs or private flows for sensitive topics. Structured ticketing, routing, and workflow automation happen without requiring employees to leave Slack. Integrating with Existing Ecosystems Integration capabilities determine whether the help desk operates as a standalone tool or connects with the broader technology stack. Connecting to CRM and Task Management Tools Zendesk offers 1,500+ marketplace apps , the deepest third-party ecosystem in the help desk market. Freshdesk provides 1,000+ apps with particularly strong connections to the Freshworks ecosystem including Freshsales and Freshchat. For internal support teams, different integrations matter: HRIS systems like Workday and Rippling for employee data sync Identity providers like Okta for access management workflows Task management like Jira and Linear for escalating technical issues Documentation platforms like Notion and Confluence for knowledge management Unthread's integration capabilities connect internal-support workflows with tools such as Asana, ClickUp, GitHub, Jira, Linear, Salesforce, HubSpot, ServiceNow, Okta, Microsoft Teams, and other business systems. The platform supports Slack Enterprise Grid for large organizations and offers SCIM sync for automated user provisioning. Ensuring Seamless Data Flow Beyond counting integrations, consider depth of connection. Surface-level integrations push notifications between systems. Deep integrations maintain bidirectional sync, trigger workflows, and share context across platforms. For internal IT teams, the ability to create Jira issues from Slack conversations, sync ticket status bidirectionally, and trigger automated responses based on Jira updates represents meaningful workflow improvement. Unthread's webhook and API enable custom integrations when pre-built connectors do not cover specific use cases. Future-Proofing Your Help Desk with AI The help desk category is shifting from ticket management systems to intelligent service platforms. Choosing the right foundation determines whether rebuilding happens in 2-3 years. Leveraging AI for Predictive Support The best help desk software no longer waits for employees to report problems. Purpose-built AI agents detect patterns, predict issues, and initiate resolutions before tickets get created. Unthread's self-learning knowledge base demonstrates this shift. Rather than requiring someone to manually write documentation, the system: Detects repeat questions from ticket history and generates draft articles for review Flags outdated documentation when ticket patterns indicate information gaps Shows clear before-after changes for one-click approval of suggested updates Syncs from existing sources including Google Drive, Notion, and web URLs This approach can reduce manual knowledge base work by drafting articles from repeated questions, flagging outdated content, and presenting suggested changes for review. Building a Self-Optimizing Knowledge Base Traditional knowledge bases decay. Documentation written during implementation becomes outdated as processes change. Teams stop trusting the knowledge base when articles no longer match reality. Self-learning systems reverse this pattern. Every resolved ticket becomes potential documentation. Every repeated question signals a content gap. The AI Analytics surface trends and gaps without requiring data analyst skills to interpret. For HR teams handling sensitive requests, Unthread offers private ticketing where employees can submit requests about payroll, parental leave, benefits, and policy questions without leaving Slack. The privacy controls ensure sensitive topics stay confidential while maintaining structured ticketing and workflow automation. Making the Right Decision Before committing to migration, teams should evaluate whether the effort addresses the fundamental challenges that drove the search for alternatives. Freshdesk offers a different pricing model and interface compared to Zendesk, but Slack-first organizations should consider whether the full request and resolution workflow can happen where employees already work. Unthread turns Slack channels into full internal help desks with structured ticketing, routing, and AI-powered automation. The platform supports IT, HR, finance, legal, and procurement teams with purpose-built workflows, integrations with business systems, and self-learning knowledge bases that reduce manual documentation work. The migration decision deserves more consideration than comparing feature lists. Request a demo to see how Slack-native help desk automation compares to traditional platforms before investing in migration. Frequently Asked Questions What data cannot be migrated using native tools? Native Freshdesk import tools only support contacts and companies. Tickets, ticket comments, attachments, knowledge base articles, automations, macros, and custom field configurations all require third-party migration tools or custom API scripts. Historical SLA performance data and detailed analytics typically cannot transfer directly and need to be archived separately before migration. How to handle open tickets during migration? Create a communication plan that sets expectations with employees about response time during transition. The recommended approach is to freeze new ticket creation in Zendesk 24-48 hours before cutover, resolve or transfer all open tickets to Freshdesk during this window, and have agents work in both systems briefly if needed. Some teams maintain parallel operation for one week, creating tickets in both systems, to ensure nothing falls through cracks. What training do agents need after migration? Most agents adapt within 1-2 days given the interface similarities between major help desk platforms. Focus training on differences in workflow automation configuration, the specific location of features agents use daily, and any changes to escalation procedures that the migration requires. Create quick reference guides for the 10-15 most common agent tasks rather than comprehensive documentation. Can integrations run on both platforms during transition? Yes, most third-party integrations like Jira, Okta, and Salesforce can connect to multiple help desk platforms simultaneously. Configure Freshdesk integrations before migration, test thoroughly with sample data, then maintain both connections during the transition period. Disable Zendesk integrations only after confirming Freshdesk connections work correctly in production. How does private HR ticketing work in Slack-native platforms? Traditional platforms require HR to maintain a separate portal or email inbox for sensitive requests, creating friction that discourages employees from using official channels. Slack-native platforms like Unthread allow employees to submit private requests through DMs or designated private channels. The request automatically creates a ticket visible only to HR team members while maintaining full audit trails, SLA tracking, and workflow automation. This approach increases adoption for sensitive topics like payroll discrepancies, accommodation requests, and interpersonal concerns. What happens to historical reporting data after migration? Most migration tools transfer ticket data but not aggregated reporting metrics. Export historical reports from Zendesk before migration and archive them for compliance and trend analysis. Freshdesk reporting starts fresh after migration, so there will be a gap in continuous metrics. Organizations requiring unbroken analytics often maintain read-only Zendesk access for 12-24 months post-migration to reference historical data.

title: Amazon OpenSearch UI now supports Network Access Control
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon OpenSearch UI now supports Network Access Control
body_text: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports network access controls for OpenSearch UI applications. OpenSearch UI is the fully managed web service for search, analytics, and unified observability across multiple AWS data sources. With network access controls, you can restrict access to your OpenSearch UI applications to approved networks using the same IAM condition keys (aws:SourceVpce, aws:SourceVpc, and aws:SourceIp) that you already use elsewhere in AWS, helping you establish a consistent data perimeter across your environment. You can enforce network restrictions at three levels: identity-based policies for specific principals, VPC endpoint policies to control which applications users reach through an endpoint, and resource control policies (RCPs) to enforce access uniformly across every account in your AWS organization. With RCPs, you can block off-network users before they authenticate, preventing anyone outside your corporate network or VPC from reaching the login page. Network access controls are available in all AWS Regions where OpenSearch UI is available. To learn more, see Restricting network access to OpenSearch UI applications in the Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide . For more information about Amazon OpenSearch Service, see the Amazon OpenSearch Service product page.
