During Q2 2026, the Company made net upfront cash payments of $4.5 billion relative to the mineral stream interests consisting of: BHP Antamina: $4.3 billion; Koné: $156 million; Spanish Mountain: $23 million; Jervois: $16 million; and Cipango: $4.5 million. Subsequent to the quarter, the Company made an additional upfront cash payment of $43.875 million relative to the El Domo mineral stream interest. Second Quarter Operating Asset Highlights Salobo: In Q2 2026, Salobo produced 62,100 ounces of attributable gold, a decrease of 11% relative to Q2 2025, primarily the result of lower grades. Antamina: In Q2 2026, Antamina produced 2.3 million ounces of attributable silver, an increase of 56% relative to Q2 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the newly acquired BHP Antamina PMPA, which increased the Company's share of silver production at Antamina from 33.75% to 67.5%, effective April 1, 2026. The benefit of the increased production share was partially offset by lower silver grades and the timing of planned maintenance, as a scheduled July maintenance shutdown was advanced into June. Lower grades were attributable to pit sequencing, with a greater proportion of copper-only ore processed during the quarter relative to copper-zinc ore, which contains more silver. Peñasquito : In Q2 2026, Peñasquito produced 1.8 million ounces of attributable silver, a decrease of 14% relative to Q2 2025, primarily the result of lower grades and recoveries resulting from planned mine sequencing, partially offset by higher throughput. Constancia : In Q2 2026, Constancia produced 0.6 million ounces of attributable silver and 3,000 ounces of attributable gold, an increase of 2% for silver production and a decrease of 35% for gold production relative to Q2 2025 . The lower gold production was the result of lower grades and recoveries, as mining activities in the higher-gold grade Pampacancha pit were completed during Q4 2025, and the remaining stockpiled Pampacancha ore was fully processed during January 2026. On July 2, 2026, Hudbay announced that it had received approval from the National Environmental Certification Service for Sustainable Investments in Perú ("SENACE") to amend its environmental permit and further increase annual mill processing capacity at Constancia. The amended permit increases the processing capacity of the Constancia mill to 34 million tonnes of ore per annum from 31 million tonnes per annum. Hudbay states that the environmental permit amendment also approves further optimization of the mine plan, extends the operational life of Constancia, and incorporates the implementation of additional infrastructure to improve tailings transport infrastructure and water management systems. Stillwater: In Q2 2026, the Stillwater mines produced 1,400 ounces of attributable gold and 2,500 ounces of attributable palladium, a decrease of 14% for gold and an increase of 3% for palladium relative to Q2 2025. The decrease in gold production was primarily a result of lower recoveries, partially offset by higher throughput, while the increase in palladium production was primarily a result of higher throughput. Blackwater: In Q2 2026, Blackwater produced 0.1 million ounces of attributable silver and 5,900 ounces of attributable gold, an increase of 7% and 46%, respectively, relative to Q2 2025, primarily the result of higher recoveries, grades and throughput. On August 4, 2026, Artemis Gold Inc. ("Artemis Gold") provided an update on the Phase 1A expansion at Blackwater, which is anticipated to increase the plant's nameplate capacity by 33%, from 6 to 8 million tonnes per annum. Artemis Gold reported that Phase 1A was 57% complete at the end of Q2 2026 and remains on schedule for commissioning in Q4 2026, with the expansion expected to contribute to production beginning in 2027. Further, Artemis Gold reported that the early works program for EP2 is nearing completion, with the first concrete pour for the ball mill foundations completed ahead of schedule. EP2 represents a significant addition to processing plant capacity above Phase 1A, and once complete, Phase 1A and EP2 are expected to expand throughput capacity to 250%, from the existing 6 Mtpa to 21 Mtpa by Q4 2028. Voisey's Bay: In Q2 2026, the Voisey's Bay mine produced 796,000 pounds of attributable cobalt, an increase of 23% relative to Q2 2025 as the underground mine at Voisey's Bay continues ramp-up to full production, with full ramp-up expected by the second half of 2026. Other Gold: In Q2 2026, total Other Gold attributable production was 5,900 ounces, an increase of 667% relative to Q2 2025 due to the addition of attributable production from the Fenix, Hemlo and Goose mines. Notable operational updates for assets included within 'Other Gold' include: Marmato: On July 29, 2026, Aris Mining ("Aris") reported that underground access connecting the Bulk Mining Zone to the new plant area is complete, with SAG and ball mills on site, and mechanical installation underway. Construction of the 5,000 tpd CIP plant continues to advance toward first gold and is on schedule for Q4 2026. Aris plans to exit 2026 operating the new CIP plant at approximately 3,000 tpd, before ramping up through 2027 to approximately 4,000 tpd by mid-2027 and the full 5,000 tpd design capacity by the end of 2027, following commissioning of the paste backfill plant. Hemlo: On July 20, 2026, Hemlo Mining Corp. ("Hemlo Mining") announced that gold production in Q2 2026 was lower than Q1 2026, reflecting a strategic refinement to the mining sequence. During the quarter, portions of the operation transitioned from a top-down to a bottom-up mining approach to reduce waste handling and improve long-term mining efficiency, resulting in delayed access to certain higher-grade stopes. Hemlo Mining expects higher production in future quarters as newly developed mining areas progress into the production sequence. Other Silver: In Q2 2026, total Other Silver attributable production was 1.6 million ounces, an increase of 19% relative to Q2 2025, primarily the result of the resumption of mining at Aljustrel and the commencement of production at Mineral Park, partially offset by lower production at Zinkgruvan. Notable operational updates for assets included within 'Other Silver' include: Aljustrel: In the third quarter of 2025, Almina resumed production of the zinc and lead concentrates at the Aljustrel mine, resulting in the resumption of attributable silver production to the Company. Los Filos: On June 25, 2026, Equinox Gold Corp. ("Equinox"), announced that it has signed 20-year land access agreements with all three communities, Carrizalillo, Mezcala and Xochipala, that host its Los Filos mine. With these agreements in place, Equinox has initiated activities to support the gradual restart of heap leach operations and to advance technical studies to evaluate potential expansion opportunities. Detailed mine-by-mine production and sales figures can be found in the Appendix to this press release and in Wheaton's consolidated MD&A in the 'Results of Operations and Operational Review' section. Recent Development Asset Updates Mineral Park : During Q2 2026, Waterton Copper LP substantially completed the commissioning stage of the mill restart. Production is expected to increase throughout the second half of the year as operations ramp up toward the mill's 16.5 Mtpa nameplate capacity. Copper concentrate sales continued in the second quarter and molybdenum concentrate sales were initiated during this quarter. Monthly delivery of silver to Wheaton under the PMPA has occurred throughout 2026. Platreef: On July 8, 2026, Ivanhoe announced that commercial production at the Platreef mine is now expected in Q4 2026. Ivanhoe states that construction of Shaft #3 was completed on schedule in late March and commissioning was finalized in June. Shaft #3 increases Platreef's hoisting capacity fivefold and enables concurrent hoisting of stoping ore and development waste. Shaft #3 is now also hoisting development waste, as the underground infrastructure is constructed in preparation for the Phase 2 expansion, which is expected to be completed by the end of 2027. In addition, stoping of higher-grade ore within the Flatreef orebody commenced at the end of the second quarter, with mining rates expected to ramp up throughout H2 2026. Fenix: On May 15, 2026, Rio2 reported that planned tonnes and grade at its Fenix mine were not achieved during Q1 2026, though the key drivers were identified early and corrective actions have been implemented or are underway. Rio2 further states that based on current ramp-up progress, they anticipate achieving commercial production in Q4 2026. Kurmuk : On July 29, 2026, Allied Gold Corporation ("Allied") announced that the previously announced agreement with Zijin Gold International Company Limited ("Zijin Gold"), where Zijin Gold was to acquire all of the issued and outstanding shares of Allied, has been terminated. Allied states further that Zijin Gold has agreed to make a strategic investment in Allied of approximately $295 million, at a subscription price representing a premium to the current market price of Allied's common shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Allied also reported that development of the Kurmuk project continued to advance during the second quarter, with the start of operations expected in August and first gold pour following a few weeks thereafter. Allied states that key execution milestones continue to be met, and the project remains on budget and on schedule while advancing commissioning activities. Koné : On June 15, 2026, Montage Gold ("Montage") reported that construction of the Koné project remains on-budget and ahead of schedule with first gold pour targeted in late Q4 2026 through the oxide circuit, while the hard-rock comminution circuit remains on track for completion in Q2 2027. Montage also reported that it has significantly exceeded its target of delineating more than 1Moz of M&I Resources at a grade at least 50% higher than that of the Koné deposit and is continuing to aggressively advance exploration through the ongoing 90,000 meter drill program, with further resource updates expected throughout the year. El Domo : On July 15, 2026, Silvercorp Metals Inc. ("Silvercorp") reported that construction advanced steadily despite rainfall challenges in the period. Advancements were achieved on infrastructure, including the non-contact water channel, processing plant foundations, and the initial tailings storage facility dam. In addition, open-pit pre-stripping activities commenced and major equipment for the processing plant and water treatment facility have been procured and shipped. Silvercorp noted that it remains focused on achieving first commissioning of the operation by July 2027, in line with the project schedule. Copper World: On July 29, 2026, Hudbay reported that the Copper World definitive feasibility study ("DFS") is progressing well, with 95% of the engineering work completed, and a sanctioning decision remains on track for later in 2026. Hudbay reports the DFS is expected to include scope for future mill expansion optionality. Santo Domingo: On July 30, 2026, Capstone Copper Corp. ("Capstone") reported that detailed engineering advanced during the second quarter, alongside continued evaluation of opportunities to optimize district infrastructure. Capstone expects to make a final investment decision on the Santo Domingo Project in Q4 2026. Kudz Ze Kayah : On July 29, 2026, BMC Minerals Ltd. ("BMC") announced that during the quarter it received receipt of a positive decision document issued by the Government of Yukon, Natural Resources Canada and the Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada, after the Yukon Environmental and Socio-economic Assessment Board had recommended approval of the project in 2020. BMC reports it will now progress mining permit and license applications with the aim to make a final investment decision in late 2027, subject to receipt of permits. Toroparu: On July 29, 2026, Aris reported that the Prefeasibility Study ("PFS") remains on schedule for completion in H2 2026, supporting a construction decision targeted for early 2027. Project optimization work in support of the PFS includes updated mine scheduling, engineering studies and other activities to advance to construction readiness. Corporate Development Jervois: On April 1, 2026, the Company entered into a PMPA with KGL (the "Jervois PMPA") for a portion of the gold and silver produced at the Jervois Project located in Australia. In return, the Company also obtained a right of first refusal on any future precious metal streams, royalties, prepays or similar transactions with respect to the Jervois Project. Under the terms of the Jervois PMPA, the Company will pay KGL total upfront cash consideration of $275 million, subject to certain customary conditions. The upfront cash consideration will be paid in a total of six installments, with the first installment of $16 million made as an early deposit payment on June 16, 2026. The second installment of $16 million is also expected to be made as an early deposit payment, once certain conditions are satisfied, and is expected to be paid in Q3 2026. The remaining balance of $243 million will be paid in four equal installments over the construction period as various conditions are satisfied. Additionally, the Company will make ongoing payments for the gold and silver ounces delivered equal to 20% of the spot price of gold and silver. Spanish Mountain: On April 20, 2026, the Company entered into a Royalty agreement with Spanish Mountain Gold (the "Spanish Mountain Royalty") for a 1.5% net smelter returns royalty on gold and silver production from the Spanish Mountain Gold Project. In return, the Company also obtained a right of first refusal on any future precious metal streams, royalties, prepays or similar transactions with respect to the Spanish Mountain Gold Project. Under the terms of the Spanish Mountain Royalty, the Company will pay Spanish Mountain Gold total upfront cash consideration of $55 million, subject to certain customary conditions. The upfront cash consideration will be paid in three installments consisting of a $22.5 million payment made on May 1, 2026, a $12.5 million payment due after 60,000 meters of drilling, and a $20 million payment due upon receiving approval under the Environmental Assessment Act (British Columbia) for the construction and operation of the project. Cipango: On June 4, 2026, the Company entered into a Royalty agreement with Cipango Limited ("Cipango Royalty") for a 1.5% net smelter returns royalty covering seven mineral exploration properties located in Japan for total upfront cash consideration of $7.5 million, subject to certain customary conditions. The Company also obtained a right of first refusal on any future precious metal streams, royalties, prepays or similar transactions with respect to such properties and an additional nine properties located in Japan. Approximately 3% of the Company's forecast 2026 production is estimated to be delivered from assets currently in construction or various stages of ramp-up. title: Reply vs. Klenty: Which should you choose in 2026?
summary: An honest 2026 comparison of Reply.io and Klenty across multichannel cadences, the Jason AI agent, deliverability, and pricing.
body_text: Reply.io and Klenty are both multichannel sequencers for small and mid-market teams. Klenty is the cleaner, cheaper cadence tool with published per-seat pricing. Reply matches it on the sequencer, from about $59 a month, and adds Jason, an AI agent for email prospecting at $500 to $800 a month. The choice turns on whether you want that agent layer. Both tools do the same core job well: run multichannel cadences across email, calls, and social outreach without the enterprise weight or price of big engagement platforms. If your motion is outbound at a reasonable scale and you want a human rep at the wheel, either one can run it. Where they diverge is the AI story on top and how each handles the details of sending. Here is the fair breakdown. For the broader category, see best email outbound tools . How Reply and Klenty compare Reply.io Klenty Best for Teams that want a value sequencer plus an AI agent option Teams that want clean, affordable multichannel cadences Sequencer Multichannel cadences from about $59/mo Multichannel cadences, published per-seat tiers AI agent Jason AI, roughly $500 to $800/mo for email prospecting No dedicated agent layer Channels Email, calls, social outreach Email, calls, social outreach Model Per-seat, human-driven Per-seat, human-driven Public pricing Sequences from $59/mo; Jason roughly $500 to $800/mo Published per-seat tiers, per its pricing page What is the difference between Reply and Klenty? At the sequencer level, they are peers. Both run multichannel cadences, both are priced for teams that do not want an enterprise contract, and both keep a rep in control of the outreach. If all you need is a clean cadence tool, you would be happy with either. The split is the AI agent. Reply layers Jason, an AI agent for email prospecting, on top of its classic sequencer, which is what pushes some buyers to Reply over Klenty. Klenty does not offer a comparable agent; it stays focused on being a strong, affordable multichannel sequencer. So the real question is whether you want an agent option inside your value sequencer, or whether you would rather keep it simple and cheaper. For broader options, see the best Reply alternatives . Which is better value for multichannel cadences? For pure cadence execution, Klenty is the tighter value pick. Its published per-seat tiers are built around clean multichannel cadences, and there is no agent premium baked in. A team that just wants email, call, and social steps running reliably tends to find Klenty does that without paying for capabilities it will not use. For related comparisons, see Apollo vs. Instantly and Apollo vs. Lemlist . Reply's base sequencer starts around $59 a month, in the same value bracket, so on the sequencer alone the two are comparable. The cost difference appears only if you add Jason. If you never turn the agent on, Reply and Klenty are close on price; if you do, Reply's total bill jumps by the $500 to $800 a month the agent costs. Match the tool to whether you will actually use the agent. For wider roundups, see the best cold email tools and best cold email marketing software . Does Reply's Jason AI agent justify the step up? It depends entirely on how much email prospecting you want to hand off. Jason brings AI-driven email prospecting on top of the sequencer, which is a real capability Klenty does not have, and for a team that wants to test agent-assisted outbound without buying a dedicated AI sales development representative (SDR) platform, it is an accessible entry point at $500 to $800 a month. The honest caveat is scope. Jason is an email-centric agent that sits on top of a classic sequencer. It does not run the whole outbound job across channels: it helps with email prospecting, but it does not source, call, and book across a full multichannel motion on its own. If email assistance is what you want, it can earn its price. If you expect it to run the entire motion, set expectations accordingly. For agency-focused picks, see the best outbound tools for agencies . Which has better deliverability and sending? Both tools invest in the fundamentals of email delivery, and neither has a decisive edge that would settle the choice on its own. Klenty and Reply each offer sending controls, inbox rotation options, and health features you would expect from a modern sequencer in this bracket. The practical advice is the same for both: run a hands-on trial against your own domains before committing, watch inbox placement on your real sending pattern, and confirm the CRM sync behaves the way your process needs. Deliverability is domain-specific and reputation-specific, so a general claim about either vendor matters less than what you see on your own mailboxes during a trial. A third option to know about Both Reply and Klenty keep a rep running the motion. A person writes the strategy, approves messages, and works replies. Reply's Jason helps with email, though it stays email-centric rather than covering the whole job. Whichever you pick, a person still owns the outbound. If you would rather the software own the motion end to end, an autonomous platform is a third path. Artisan built Ava, an autonomous AI business development representative (BDR) , to source, write, send, call, reply, and book on her own across email, social media, and dialer steps, priced on work performed instead of per seat. That is a different purchase from a value sequencer with an agent add-on, and it fits teams that want the outcome instead of a tool to drive. See artisan.co/pricing for the model. Choose Reply if... You want a value sequencer with the option to add an AI email-prospecting agent. Jason's agent-assisted email fits how you want to test AI outbound without a full AI SDR platform. You are comfortable with the step up to $500 to $800 a month when you turn the agent on. You want an accessible on-ramp to agent-run email inside a familiar sequencer. Multichannel cadences from about $59 a month cover your base needs. Choose Klenty if... You want clean, affordable multichannel cadences without paying for an agent layer. Published per-seat pricing and predictable costs matter to you. Your motion is human-driven and you want a rep at the wheel by design. You found bigger engagement platforms overbuilt for your needs. Email, call, and social steps running reliably is the whole ask. Frequently asked questions Is Reply or Klenty cheaper? On the base sequencer, they are close. Reply's sequences start around $59 a month, and Klenty publishes comparable per-seat tiers. The gap opens only if you add Reply's Jason AI agent, which runs roughly $500 to $800 a month. So if you use only the sequencer, expect similar costs; if you want Jason, Reply becomes meaningfully more expensive. Match the choice to whether you will actually use the agent. What does Reply's Jason AI agent do that Klenty cannot? Jason adds AI-driven email prospecting on top of Reply's sequencer, a capability Klenty does not offer. It helps generate and run email prospecting with less manual work. The limit is scope: Jason is an email-centric agent on a classic sequencer, and it does not run a full multichannel motion autonomously. If email assistance is what you want, it is a real advantage; do not expect it to own the whole job. Which is better for multichannel cadences? Both run email, call, and social outreach cadences well, so this is close. Klenty is the tighter value pick if you want clean multichannel execution without an agent premium. Reply matches the multichannel base and adds the Jason option. For pure cadence execution at the lowest predictable cost, Klenty tends to win; for cadences plus an AI email option, Reply does. Are Reply and Klenty good for enterprise teams? Both are value sequencers aimed at small and mid-market teams instead of large enterprises. They lack the deep governance, permissions, and reporting depth that dedicated enterprise engagement platforms offer. A large, disciplined sales org usually needs more control than either provides. For a smaller team that wants affordable multichannel cadences with a rep in charge, both fit well. Is there an alternative to both Reply and Klenty? Yes. Both are human-driven: a rep writes the strategy, approves messages, and works replies, and Reply's Jason agent only assists with email. If you want the software to own the outbound job end to end, Artisan's Ava is an autonomous AI BDR that sources, writes, sends, calls, replies, and books across channels on her own, priced on work performed instead of per seat. It is a different category than a value sequencer, suited to teams that want the motion run for them instead of assisted. Should I trial both before deciding? Yes. Because the base sequencers are close and deliverability is domain-specific, a hands-on trial on your own mailboxes is the best tiebreaker. Test inbox placement on your real sending pattern, confirm CRM sync fits your process, and if you are considering Reply, evaluate whether Jason's email prospecting justifies the added cost before you commit to it. body_text: Az online kaszinók világa ma már jóval többet jelent néhány digitális nyerőgépnél. A felnőtt közönség számára kialakított szórakoztató felületeken különböző hangulatok, játéktípusok és látványvilágok sorakoznak egymás mellett, így minden látogatás másféle élményt kínálhat. Van, aki a klasszikus eleganciát keresi, más a filmszerű történeteket, a gyors ritmust vagy éppen a valódi kaszinóterem hangulatát értékeli. A választék első pillantásra nagynak tűnhet, de általában jól áttekinthető csoportokba rendezik. A kezdőoldalakon kiemelt újdonságok, népszerű címek és tematikus válogatások jelennek meg, miközben külön menüpontok segítenek eligazodni a különböző játékcsaládok között. Az online szórakoztató felületek technológiai hátteréről és fejlődéséről az https://innovationandsecurity.hu/ oldalon is találhatók hasznos, általános információk. A klasszikus játékok időtlen hangulata A hagyományos kaszinójátékok digitális változatai azoknak lehetnek érdekesek, akik kedvelik az egyszerű, könnyen felismerhető megjelenést. A kártyalapok, a zsetonok, a zöld posztó és a visszafogott díszítések azonnal megteremtik a kaszinók világának jellegzetes hangulatát. Ezek a címek ritkán akarnak történetet mesélni vagy túlzottan látványosak lenni; inkább a letisztult megjelenés és az ismerős atmoszféra áll a középpontban. A klasszikus kínálatban gyakran különféle rulettváltozatok, kártyaalapú játékok és egyszerűbb asztali szórakozások szerepelnek. Ami igazán kiemelkedik, az a változatosság apró részletekben: eltérő asztaltervek, zenei aláfestések, animációk és eltérő tempójú felületek adnak saját karaktert az egyes változatoknak. Aki a nyugodtabb, elegánsabb élményt kedveli, rendszerint ebben a kategóriában találja meg a legkellemesebb látványvilágot. klasszikus asztali játékok letisztult megjelenéssel; hagyományos kártyajátékok modern grafikai környezetben; élő közvetítésű asztalok valós osztókkal és teremhangulattal. A nyerőgépek mint mini történetvilágok A digitális nyerőgépek kínálata sokkal színesebb, mint azt a régi, néhány szimbólumos gépek alapján gondolnánk. A mai címek gyakran önálló témára épülnek: mitológiai kalandokra, tenger alatti világokra, zenére, utazásra, gasztronómiára vagy éppen futurisztikus városokra. A játékélmény fontos része a látvány, a hang és az animáció, ezért egy jól megtervezett cím szinte rövid jelenetként működik. Ebben a kategóriában a felfedezés örömét elsősorban a tematika adja. Egyik cím elegáns és visszafogott, a másik harsány, humoros vagy filmes hangulatú. Sok felületen külön válogatás mutatja az új megjelenéseket, a visszatérő kedvenceket és az adott időszakhoz kapcsolódó tematikus játékokat. A választékot az is gazdagítja, hogy ugyanazon alapötlet többféle grafikai stílusban és eltérő hangulatban jelenhet meg. Ami különösen figyelemre méltó, az a részletek kidolgozása. A szimbólumok nem puszta képek, hanem a választott történetvilág részei, a hanghatások pedig sokszor fokozatosan építik fel az atmoszférát. Egyes címek szinte rajzfilmszerűek, mások komolyabb, mozis megjelenést kínálnak. Ezért a nyerőgépek között nemcsak játéktípus, hanem vizuális ízlés alapján is könnyű különbséget tenni. Élő kaszinó: amikor a képernyő teremmé változik Az élő kaszinó kategória egyik legerősebb vonzereje a közvetlenség. A stúdióból vagy valódi kaszinóteremből sugárzott asztaloknál osztók és más résztvevők jelennek meg, ami sokkal személyesebb benyomást kelthet, mint egy kizárólag animációkra épülő felület. A többkamerás közvetítés, a rendezett díszlet és a folyamatosan látható asztal együtt olyan érzést ad, mintha a néző közelebb kerülne a kaszinók klasszikus világához. Az élő formátumok hangulata különösen változatos. Vannak elegáns, sötétebb tónusú stúdiók, amelyek a luxusszállodák atmoszféráját idézik, és léteznek világosabb, modernebb környezetek is, ahol a közvetítés gyorsabbnak és lazábbnak hat. A kezelőfelület általában kiegészítő információkat, több kameraállást és jól elkülönített asztalokat kínál, így a hangsúly a jelenlét élményén marad. Tematikus válogatások és digitális kényelem A jó online kaszinófelület nemcsak sok játékot kínál, hanem segít felfedezni a kínálat karakterét is. A tematikus gyűjtemények, a műfaj szerinti bontás és a látványos borítóképek megkönnyítik az összehasonlítást. Egy különleges zenei világ, egy történelmi korszak vagy egy népszerű filmes motívum alapján gyorsan kirajzolódhat, milyen jellegű élmények dominálnak az adott oldalon. A használhatóság szintén sokat számít. A rendezett menük, a gyorsan betöltődő képernyők és a mobiltelefonon is jól működő megjelenés kényelmesebbé teszi a nézelődést. A modern felületek gyakran nagy hangsúlyt helyeznek a hangulatváltásra: néhány mozdulattal át lehet térni a klasszikus asztaloktól a látványos nyerőgépekhez, majd az élő közvetítésekhez. Ettől a kínálat nem kaotikusnak, hanem folyamatosan felfedezhetőnek érződik. Összességében az online kaszinó szórakoztató ereje a sokféleségben rejlik. A klasszikus játékok eleganciája, a tematikus nyerőgépek kreativitása és az élő kaszinó közvetlensége egymást kiegészítve alkotnak változatos digitális világot. A legérdekesebb felületek nem egyetlen stílusra építenek, hanem többféle hangulatot kínálnak a felnőtt közönségnek, miközben az élmény középpontjában végig a látvány, a hangulat és a választék felfedezése marad.

title: Rocket Lab Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results: Posts Record Revenue and Record Backlog, Guides To Another Record Revenue Quarter in Q3 2026
summary: LONG BEACH, Calif., Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today shared the financial results for fiscal second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Rocket Lab founder and CEO, Sir Peter Beck, says: “Q2 was another
body_text: Rocket Lab Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results: Posts Record Revenue and Record Backlog, Guides To Another Record Revenue Quarter in Q3 2026 August 10, 2026 PDF Version LONG BEACH, Calif., Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today shared the financial results for fiscal second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Rocket Lab founder and CEO, Sir Peter Beck, says: “Q2 was another fantastic quarter for Rocket Lab, highlighted by record results and massive momentum that has continued well after the close. We achieved a record $234 million in Q2 revenue - up 62% year-over-year and $34 million higher than last quarter’s record - driven by surging demand across all areas of our business. Q2 2026 saw our backlog grow to $2.36 billion – another record – which, combined with new deals in the period since, equates to more than $1 billion1 in new contracts across launch and space systems already entered into in Q3.” “Alongside this execution, we closed the acquisitions of Mynaric and Motiv and announced our historic deal to acquire Iridium Communications Inc. Together, these moves position Rocket Lab to accelerate our future into space applications by becoming a self-launching, tier-1 space power that will deliver critical communications capability to millions of users worldwide.” Highlights for the Second Quarter 2026, plus business updates since June 30, 2026. Record quarterly revenue of $234 million, a 62% increase YoY. Record backlog of $2.36 billion, a 137% increase YoY. Announced a landmark agreement to acquire Iridium to create a fully vertically-integrated space powerhouse that designs, builds, launches, and operates its own constellations, delivering critical communications capability to millions of users worldwide. Secured more than $437 million[1] in new launch contracts across its Electron, HASTE, and Neutron launch vehicles during Q2 2026 plus post-quarter signings, expanding Rocket Lab’s total launch backlog to its highest in history with 90+ launches. Introduced the Company’s GHOST globally-deployable launch system to support suborbital and orbital launches from anywhere in the world. GHOST’s first location – named Rocket Lab Launch Complex 4 - will be at the Pacific Spaceport Complex at Kodiak, Alaska, with two pads to be established for high-frequency launch campaigns. The system is set to make its operational debut with a suborbital launch from Alaska in 2027. Achieved critical milestones across Neutron’s assembly, integration, and testing of first-flight hardware as Rocket Lab progresses toward the inaugural launch of its medium-lift reusable rocket. Production of the Stage 1 tank is currently aligned with the target delivery of Neutron to the launch pad in Q4 2026. Awarded a $3972 million contract to deliver multiple Flatellite spacecraft to launch on Neutron for the U.S. Space Force’s Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator (SB-AMTI) program: a critically-important mission for national security to detect, track, and monitor airborne threats from space. Rocket Lab is one of only two vendors delivering launch-plus-spacecraft for SB-AMTI: a compelling recognition of the value of Rocket Lab’s strategic vertical integration. Awarded more than $160 million across two contracts to build three geostationary satellites. The deals include a prime contract with the Space Force’s Space Systems Command to build and operate two satellites for space domain awareness, representing Rocket Lab’s first foray into geostationary satellite production and operation for the U.S. Government. Formally established Rocket Lab Germany GmbH to support potential future scaling of Rocket Lab satellite and component manufacturing in Germany and provide commercial and sovereign space capabilities to European customers. Third Quarter 2026 Guidance For the third quarter of 2026, Rocket Lab expects: Revenue between $250 million and $265 million. GAAP Gross Margins between 29% and 31%. Non-GAAP Gross Margins between 35% and 37%. GAAP Operating Expenses between $143 million and $149 million. Non-GAAP Operating Expenses between $121 million and $127 million. Interest Income, net $21 million. Adjusted EBITDA loss of between $17 million and $23 million. Basic Weighted Average Common Shares Outstanding of 641 million, including approximately 41 million of Series A Convertible Participating Preferred Shares. See “Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below for an explanation of our use of Non-GAAP financial measures, and the reconciliation of historical Non-GAAP measures to the comparable GAAP measures in the tables attached to this press release. We have not provided a reconciliation for the forward-looking Non-GAAP Gross Margin, Non-GAAP Operating Expenses or Adjusted EBITDA expectations for Q3 2026 described above because, without unreasonable efforts, we are unable to predict with reasonable certainty the amount and timing of adjustments that are used to calculate these non-GAAP financial measures, particularly related to stock-based compensation and its related tax effects. Stock-based compensation is currently expected to range from $18 million to $20 million in Q3 2026. ________________________________ 1 Includes options across various contracts. 2 Includes options across various contracts. Conference Call Information Rocket Lab will host a conference call for investors at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET) today to discuss these business highlights and financial results for our second quarter, other updates, and to provide our outlook for the third quarter 2026. The live webcast and a replay of the webcast will be available on Rocket Lab’s Investor Relations website: https://investors.rocketlabcorp.com/ Rocket Lab Investor Relations Contact Patrick Vorenkamp investors@rocketlabusa.com Rocket Lab Media Contact Murielle Baker media@rocketlabusa.com About Rocket Lab Rocket Lab (Nasdaq: RKLB) is an end-to-end space company delivering rockets, satellites, and spacecraft components for commercial, government, and defense missions. Driven by its industry-leading small-lift rockets Electron and HASTE and its upcoming reusable Neutron medium-lift rocket, Rocket Lab delivers reliable and responsive launch for the world’s most important missions from constellation deployment to missile defense. Rocket Lab’s satellites and components have powered more than 1,700 missions in Earth orbit, as well as deep-space exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Learn more at www.rocketlabcorp.com . title: What Is a Rainscreen? Understanding the Layer Behind Advanced Moisture Management
summary: Learn the basics of rainscreen design, how moisture management impacts wall performance, and how LP® products fit into modern exterior wall assemblies.
body_text: When most people think about a home's exterior, they only focus on the material they see on the outside. But behind every high-performing exterior wall system is a series of components working together to manage moisture and help protect the structure. One term that's becoming increasingly common in residential and commercial construction is rainscreen . While it's often associated with modern, high-performance building design, many homeowners and even some builders may not fully understand what a rainscreen is, how it works, or when it might be beneficial. What Is a Rainscreen? A rainscreen is a wall design approach that creates a drainage and ventilation space between the siding and the wall assembly behind it. Rather than relying on the siding alone to keep water out, a rainscreen system recognizes that wind-driven rain and moisture can occasionally get behind exterior cladding. The goal is to provide a pathway for that moisture to drain and dry before it impacts the wall assembly. A typical rainscreen assembly includes: Exterior cladding (such as siding) An air gap or drainage cavity A water-resistive barrier (WRB) Structural wall sheathing and framing Together, these components help manage water, improve drying potential, and support long-term wall performance. Why Moisture Management Matters Moisture is one of the biggest threats to a building's durability. When water becomes trapped within a wall assembly, it can contribute to: Fungal decay Mold and mildew growth Reduced insulation performance Premature material deterioration That's why modern building science focuses on managing moisture rather than assuming it can be completely prevented. A properly designed wall assembly gives water a way to escape and allows the wall to dry if moisture does get inside. How Does a Rainscreen Work? Think of a rainscreen like a drainage plane behind your siding. When rain hits the exterior of a home: The siding acts as the first line of defense. Any moisture that gets behind the cladding can drain downward through the cavity. Air movement within the cavity helps promote drying. The water-resistive barrier provides an additional layer of protection for the structure. This layered approach helps create a more resilient building envelope. Do All Homes Need a Rainscreen? Building requirements vary by climate, wall design, local codes, and project goals. In areas that experience frequent rainfall, high humidity, or significant wind-driven rain, builders may choose rainscreen assemblies to improve moisture management and drying potential. Many architects and building professionals incorporate rainscreen principles into high-performance wall systems because they can help support long-term durability. Since every project is different, builders should always follow local code requirements, manufacturer installation instructions, and project specifications. Where Do LP® Products Fit? It's important to understand that LP does not manufacture or sell a complete rainscreen system. However, LP products can be incorporated into wall assemblies that utilize rainscreen design principles. LP WeatherLogic® Air & Water Barrier LP WeatherLogic® panels provide integrated structural sheathing and an air and water barrier in a single panel. When installed according to LP instructions, they can help create a continuous layer of protection within the wall assembly. LP® SmartSide® Trim & Siding LP SmartSide products serve as the exterior cladding layer of the wall system. When installed as part of a properly designed assembly, they can contribute to a durable and attractive exterior while working alongside the other components responsible for moisture management. Benefits of a Well-Designed Wall Assembly Whether or not a project includes a dedicated rainscreen system, builders increasingly focus on creating walls that effectively manage moisture and support long-term performance. Potential benefits of a well-designed assembly include: Improved moisture management Enhanced drying potential Long-term durability Advanced protection of structural components Increased confidence in varying weather conditions The Bottom Line A rainscreen is not a product—it's a building design strategy that helps manage moisture behind exterior cladding. As building science continues to evolve, many builders and designers are incorporating rainscreen principles into their wall assemblies to help improve durability and moisture control. While LP does not offer a complete rainscreen system, LP WeatherLogic® and LP® SmartSide® products can be incorporated into wall assemblies designed to support modern moisture-management practices. By understanding how these components work together, builders and homeowners can make more informed decisions about creating durable, high-performing exterior wall systems. For more information on LP Products, visit https://www.lpcorp.com/ .

title: Cement producer hires AVG Logistics for electric truck logistics in North East India
summary: Cement producer hires AVG Logistics for electric truck logistics in North East India
body_text: India: AVG Logistics has won a five-year contract worth US$1.89m/yr, extendable by three years, to deploy 30 electric heavy-goods vehicles for a cement producer's inbound and outbound transport of raw materials and cement. title: Elicio Therapeutics Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Updates | Elicio Therapeutics
summary: August 13, 2026 16:01 ETFollowing the observation of multiple complete responses, Elicio plans to initiate a Phase 1 combination study of ELI-002 7P plus a ...
body_text: August 13, 2026 16:01 ET Following the observation of multiple complete responses, Elicio plans to initiate a Phase 1 combination study of ELI-002 7P plus a RAS small molecule inhibitor with or without an anti-PD-1 inhibitor in metastatic pancreatic cancer; Phase 1 study anticipated to initiate Q4 2026 While Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial did not meet its primary endpoint, Elicio continues to evaluate pre-specified subgroups, including the R0 resected population, to further refine its Phase 3 development strategy for ELI-002 7P in adjuvant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (“PDAC”) Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center-led Phase 1 trial activated evaluating ELI-002 7P plus chemotherapy and checkpoint inhibition with treatment initiating in neoadjuvant pancreatic cancer and continuing post-resection $15 million financing in July 2026, strengthens balance sheet to support cash runway into Q1 2027 BOSTON, Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Elicio Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: ELTX, “Elicio” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a pipeline of next-generation immunotherapies for KRAS-driven cancers, today reported financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided recent corporate and clinical updates. “The encouraging clinical observations reported to date, including multiple complete responses following ELI-002 7P treatment and subsequent checkpoint inhibition, further support the promise of our AMP platform approach and its potential to generate durable anti-tumor immune responses,” said Robert Connelly, Chief Executive Officer of Elicio. “Our recent financing provided us with the capital needed to evaluate initial data from our planned Phase 1 combination study of ELI-002 7P with a RAS small molecule inhibitor with or without an anti-PD-1 inhibitor, which is anticipated to begin in the fourth quarter of this year. We are excited to advance our combination strategy and hope to unlock the full potential of our AMP platform to deliver durable clinical benefit for patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer.” Recent Highlights Reported multiple complete responses following ELI-002 7P treatment and subsequent checkpoint inhibition in metastatic mKRAS pancreatic cancer, which Elicio believes supports the planned Phase 1 combination study. Reported results from the Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial for ELI-002 7P in adjuvant mKRAS-driven pancreatic cancer following completion of standard locoregional therapy. The trial did not meet the primary endpoint but Elicio continues to evaluate pre-specified subgroups, including the R0 resected population, to further refine its Phase 3 development strategy for ELI-002 7P in adjuvant PDAC. Announced the activation of an investigator-initiated Phase 1 neoadjuvant trial evaluating ELI-002 7P plus chemotherapy and an anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor in borderline resectable and resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (“PDAC”). The multi-center study is being led by Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and funded through a strategic partnership between The Lustgarten Foundation and Break Through Cancer. Published a peer-reviewed manuscript in Science Advances highlighting the potent and durable immune responses generated by certain amphiphile (“AMP”)-DNA adjuvant candidates developed using the Company’s lymph node-targeting AMP platform technology. Completed a $15.0 million registered direct offering led by new institutional investors to support the planned Phase 1 development of ELI-002 7P in metastatic pancreatic cancer and advance the Company’s pipeline. Added to the Russell 2000® and Russell 3000® Indexes, broadening visibility among institutional investors and index-based funds. Upcoming Anticipated Milestones Initiation of the Phase 1 combination trial for ELI-002 7P in combination with a RAS small molecule inhibitor with or without an anti-PD-1 inhibitor in metastatic mKRAS pancreatic cancer anticipated in Q4 2026 Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results R&D expense for the second quarter of 2026 was $6.8 million, compared to $7.0 million for the second quarter of 2025. The decrease of $0.2 million was primarily due to lower clinical trial costs as the Phase 2 study of ELI-002 7P continued and the patients moved out of the active dosing phase and into the follow up phase of the trial. G&A expense for the second quarter of 2026 was $3.6 million, compared to $3.1 million for the second quarter of 2025. The increase of $0.5 million was primarily due to increased Company headcount resulting in increased personnel costs and a slight increase in professional fees. Net loss for the second quarter of 2026 was $8.2 million, compared to $10.6 million for the second quarter of 2025. Net loss per share for the second quarter of 2026 was $0.43 compared to $0.66 for the second quarter of 2025. Cash and cash equivalents were $23.5 million as of June 30, 2026. The Company raised net proceeds of $16.6 million in the second quarter of 2026, for aggregate net proceeds of approximately $24.4 million year to date, through its established at-the-market program. In July 2026, the Company raised aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $15.0 million in a registered direct offering before deducting the placement agents’ fees and related offering expenses. The Company expects that its current cash and cash equivalents will support operations into the first quarter of 2027. ELICIO THERAPEUTICS, INC. (Nasdaq: ELTX) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing next-generation immunotherapies for the treatment of KRAS-driven cancers, including mKRAS-positive pancreatic and colorectal cancers. Elicio intends to build on recent clinical findings in the personalized cancer immunotherapy space to develop effective, off-the-shelf immunotherapies. Elicio’s AMP technology aims to enhance the education, activation and amplification of cancer-specific T cells relative to conventional immunotherapy strategies, with the goal of promoting durable cancer immunosurveillance in patients. Elicio’s ELI-002 7P lead program is an off-the-shelf immunotherapy candidate targeting the most common KRAS mutations, which drive approximately 25% of all solid tumors. Off-the-shelf immunotherapy approaches have the potential benefits of low cost, rapid commercial scale manufacturing, and rapid availability of drug to patients, especially in neo-adjuvant settings and for prophylaxis in high-risk patients, contrary to personalized immunotherapy approaches. Elicio’s pipeline includes additional off-the-shelf therapeutic cancer immunotherapy candidates, including ELI-007 and ELI-008, that target BRAF-driven cancers and p53 hotspot mutations, respectively. About ELI-002 Elicio’s lead product candidate, ELI-002, is a structurally novel investigational AMP cancer immunotherapy that targets cancers that are driven by mutations in the KRAS-gene—a prevalent driver of many human cancers. ELI-002 is comprised of two powerful components that are built with Elicio’s proprietary AMP technology consisting of AMP-modified mutant KRAS peptide antigens and ELI-004, an AMP-modified CpG oligodeoxynucleotide adjuvant that is available as an off-the-shelf subcutaneous administration. ELI-002 7P (7-peptide formulation) was evaluated in the randomized Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial in patients with mKRAS-driven pancreatic cancer (NCT05726864). The Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial included patients with mKRAS-positive pancreatic cancer who completed standard therapy but remain at high risk of relapse. Elicio continues to evaluate pre-specified subgroups, including the R0 resected population, and intends to further refine its Phase 3 development strategy for ELI-002 7P in adjuvant PDAC. Elicio intends to initiate a Phase 1 study in metastatic PDAC designed to provide a rapid assessment of clinical activity using an open label design to assess the objective response rate including partial and complete radiographic responses. Elicio plans to use the study findings to further evaluate checkpoint inhibitor combinations and help inform future development strategies in metastatic PDAC and the adjuvant PDAC Phase 3 trial. At the time of the Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P analysis, data for overall survival remained immature. ELI-002 also has been studied in patients with mKRAS-positive colorectal cancer in Phase 1 studies. In the future, Elicio may seek to expand ELI-002 7P to other indications, including mKRAS-positive lung cancer and other mKRAS-positive cancers, subject to financing. The ELI-002 7P formulation is designed to provide immune response coverage against seven of the most common KRAS mutations present in 25% of all solid tumors, thereby increasing the potential patient population for ELI-002. About the Amphiphile Platform Elicio’s proprietary AMP platform delivers investigational immunotherapeutics directly to the “brain center” of the immune system – the lymph nodes. Elicio believes this site-specific delivery of disease-specific antigens, adjuvants and other immunomodulators may efficiently educate, activate and amplify critical immune cells, potentially resulting in induction and persistence of potent adaptive immunity required to treat many diseases. In pre-clinical models, Elicio observed lymph node-specific engagement driving therapeutic immune responses of increased magnitude, function and durability. Elicio believes its AMP lymph node-targeted approach will produce superior clinical benefits compared to immunotherapies that do not engage the lymph nodes based on preclinical studies. Elicio’s AMP platform, originally developed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, has broad potential in the cancer space to advance a number of development initiatives through internal activities, in-licensing arrangements or development collaborations and partnerships. The AMP platform has been shown to deliver immunotherapeutics directly to the lymph nodes by latching on to the protein albumin, found in the local injection site, as it travels to lymphatic tissue. title: How to compare two Word documents
summary: Straining your eyes to spot the difference between two documents? Here's how to compare two Word documents. Plus, how to compare documents in Google Docs.
body_text: I used to compare two documents by positioning them side by side on one small screen and then manually scanning for errors, sentence by sentence. As you'd expect, that method morphed my face into an alarming scrunch, and more importantly, it was ripe for human error. Then I learned that every word processing app I use has a built-in tool to do exactly this. If you're straining your eyes to spot the difference between two documents, here's how to compare two Word documents in the desktop app. Note: There's no built-in tool to compare documents in the web version of Word. Table of contents : How to compare two Word documents How to merge Word documents How to compare two Word documents side by side How to compare documents in Google Docs How to merge documents in Google Docs How to compare documents and files using free tools How to compare two Word documents Microsoft makes it really easy to compare two Word documents in the desktop app, but it isn't immediately obvious. Open a new document in Word. In the upper ribbon, click Review . Click Compare , and then click Compare Documents . In the Compare Documents window that appears, update the following fields: Original document : Choose the first document you want to use in your comparison. Revised document : Choose the other version of the document that you want to use in your comparison. Label changes with: To make it easier to spot differences, assign a label—for example, the writer's name—to mark changes in the revised document. In: By default, Word will display changes between the two documents in the original document. I prefer to compare documents in a new document in case I ever want to revert back to the original of either version. To do this, click New document in the Show Changes section. (If this option isn't visible, click the down caret [∨].) Click OK . Word then merges the two documents together and tracks differences as comments in the Markup Area in the side panel of the doc. If you're scanning through just the doc, Word also applies a red font color and underlines any differences in text. How to merge Word documents Let's say you want to incorporate all the changes from the second version into the original document, without the markups. Here's how to quickly do this after you've compared both documents. Click the down caret ( ∨ ) next to Accept in the Review tab. Click Accept All Changes . Or, you can click Accept and Move to Next to manually review each change and merge select edits. If you compare two documents in a new document, Word takes changes from the Revised document (the second file) and merges them into the Original document. And if you want to merge Word documents without comparing them first, here's how. Click Review in the upper ribbon. Click Compare , and then click Combine Documents . In the Combine Documents window that appears, select the two documents you want to combine. Click OK . When you're done, don't forget to hit the Ctrl+S shortcut to save your changes. Compare vs. combine in Word: What's the difference? Where compare lets you easily see the differences between two documents, combine lets you merge two documents with different changes made by multiple editors into a single document. Use combine when you already have edits (tracked changes) in the drafts. Neither of these features is available on Word for Web because the online version tracks changes similarly to Google Docs . How to compare two Word documents side by side If you prefer to do visual gymnastics, you can also compare two Word documents side by side. Open the two Word documents you want to compare. In either of the documents, click View . In the Window group, click View Side by Side . (You might only see the icon for it, which looks like two documents next to each other.) Optionally, click Synchronous Scrolling to scroll both documents at the same time. Once you're done comparing documents, click View Side by Side again to return to your normal, single file view. How to compare documents in Google Docs The steps to compare two documents in Google Docs varies slightly from Word, but it's just as straightforward to do. Open the first document you want to compare. In the menu, click Tools , and then click Compare documents . In the Compare documents window that appears, select the second document you want to use in your comparison, and enter a name in the Attribute differences to field. You can even include comments from the second document. Then click Compare . In the Comparison is ready window that appears, click Open . This will create a new document. (Unlike Word, there's no option to populate changes into the original document.) Similar to Word, any differences between the two documents are tracked in suggestion mode as Google Docs comments . And to give you an at-a-glance view of differences directly in the doc, Google Docs treats changes with a different font color. How to merge documents in Google Docs Google Docs doesn't have a dedicated tool to combine two documents. But there is a workaround. Follow the above steps to compare documents. In the new document's menu, click Tools , then click Review suggested edits . To accept all the suggested edits at once, click Accept All . If you want to manually review each suggestion first, click the up (∧) or down (∨) caret next to Suggested edits , and the Accept All button will automatically change to Accept . Now you can accept edits one at a time. You can also preview what your document would look like if you accepted all the edits. Click the down caret (v) next to Show suggested edits , and then select Preview "Accept all." That way, you can look at the document before you end up having to manually correct weird capitalization or other formatting issues. How to compare documents and files using free tools Let's say you want to quickly compare two versions of text that weren't originally drafted in Word or Google Docs. There are online tools designed to do just this. Some even let you compare PDFs, PowerPoint presentations, and code. Here are three document and file comparison tools you can use for free. Draftable Draftable is a ridiculously easy-to-use free tool that lets you compare Word documents, PowerPoint presentations (only .ppt , not .pptx ), and PDFs. Upload your two files, click Compare , and in seconds, you'll have a side-by-side comparison with differences highlighted directly in the doc and listed to the side (similar to Word and Google Docs). QuickDiff If you have only plain text to compare—as in, no formatting like bold and underline or elements like tables and hyperlinks—then QuickDiff is a decent option. Copy and paste the two bits of text you want to compare, and then click Check for differences . You can even tell QuickDiff to ignore changes like inserted or deleted blank lines and letter case. There are a few downsides to QuickDiff worth mentioning. Spots errors at a sentence or paragraph level only . QuickDiff highlights entire sections (sentences or paragraphs) that contain differences. This means that if there are minor changes within any given sentence or paragraph, you still have to manually review that section to find the difference. Limited accessibility . QuickDiff uses only visual cues to highlight differences, which isn't helpful if you have limited vision. Diffchecker Diffchecker is a full file comparison tool that can highlight differences in code, documents, and images. It has a web app, but you can also buy the desktop version if you want to avoid uploading your documents to the platform's cloud servers. The platform relies on optical character recognition (OCR) to scan PDFs, compare images, and scan multiple Excel documents. To scan full folders, you'll need to pay for the Pro version, which starts at $21/user/month. Here are some of the downsides of choosing Diffchecker: There's no mobile support. Diffchecker doesn't have a mobile application for "on-the-go" document checking. The desktop version requires payment. The free version requires you to upload documents or paste text individually, while the desktop version lets you access files without uploading them to a cloud server. Play spot the difference for fun—not for work I love a good game of Spot the difference when it's strictly for entertainment (or a cheesy participation ribbon). But the stakes are infinitely higher when you need to do it in a professional capacity. Don't risk the chance of human error—or scaring off your coworkers if you make the same furiously scrunched face I do. Use your word processor's built-in features or an online comparison tool to spot the differences for you. And whether you're using Word's built-in compare tool, Google Docs, or a dedicated app, catching every edit is only half the battle—the other half is making sure the right version ends up in the right place. Zapier lets you connect your favorite word processor to the rest of your stack to automatically archive finalized drafts, alert teammates when a document's ready for review, or route approved edits straight into your CMS or project management tool. Automate the process, or access and make changes to your documents straight from your AI assistant. Try Zapier Related reading: New Google Docs features to try How to edit a PDF on Windows How to convert Word docs into Google Docs How to make a flowchart in Word How to merge PDF files This article was originally published in August 2023. title: ZYRTEC® launches new drug-free allergen shield spray, a breakthrough for proactive everyday* allergen defense
summary: New nasal mist helps block airborne allergens before they trigger allergy symptoms, by forming a protective barrier in the nose.
body_text: ZYRTEC™ Allergen Shield Spray is a first-of-its-kind nasal mist from ZYRTEC®, the #1 doctor and allergist recommended oral OTC allergy brand and the leading allergy brand with consumers. The drug-free nasal spray helps combat allergy symptoms before they start** by forming a protective barrier in the nose to help block allergens, including pollen, pet dander and dust. Starts blocking allergens in minutes and provides up to six hours of protection. Expands the ZYRTEC® portfolio with a new option for proactive allergen defense. SUMMIT, NJ – [August 18, 2026] – ZYRTEC®, the #1 doctor and allergist recommended oral over-the-counter (OTC) allergy relief brand, announced the launch of ZYRTEC™ Allergen Shield Spray, a breakthrough in proactive allergen defense. Scientifically proven to help reduce allergy symptoms, the drug-free nasal spray gives consumers a new way to manage and defend against allergies. The gentle nasal mist begins working in minutes, forming a protective gel barrier in the nose that helps block common allergens before they can cause symptoms. It’s ideal for use before activities like spending time outdoors, mowing the lawn or visiting friends with pets. ZYRTEC™ Allergen Shield Spray is a complementary product to your allergy toolkit, designed to help millions of allergy sufferers take a more proactive approach to allergen defense. “As a leader in allergy relief, we saw an opportunity to innovate and offer consumers a new way to prepare for allergy season,” said Jenn Lovell, Head of US Allergy, Kenvue. “ZYRTEC™ Allergen Shield Spray expands the allergy toolkit with a drug-free option that helps block allergens before they can trigger allergy symptoms, empowering consumers to take a more proactive approach to managing their allergies.” How ZYRTEC™ Allergen Shield Spray Technology Works Much like applying sunscreen before sun exposure, ZYRTEC™ Allergen Shield Spray is designed to be used before allergen exposure, creating a lightweight physical barrier in the nose to help reduce contact with common airborne allergens. A Drug-Free Formula: Formulated with Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose (HPMC), a plant-derived ingredient that forms a lightweight barrier in the nose. Traps Allergens: Forms a physical barrier in the nose that helps trap allergen particles in minutes. Shields in Minutes: Blocks allergens such as pollen, pet dander and dust, and provides up to six hours of protection. ZYRTEC™ Allergen Shield Spray is intended for adults and children ages 12 and older and is now available at major U.S. retailers nationwide and online wherever ZYRTEC® products are sold. Consumers can learn more at Zyrtec.com. *Based on a 4-week clinical trial. Can be used up to 3x daily, as needed and only as directed. **When used before allergen exposure. About ZYRTEC® As the #1 doctor and allergist recommended oral over-the-counter allergy relief brand, ZYRTEC® is here to help you take control of your indoor and outdoor allergies. ZYRTEC® provides superior allergy care to empower you to live a more connected everyday life, unburdened by allergies.

title: Cybersecurity and Rural Health Tech Investments Drive This Week's SLED News
summary: This Week's SLED News
body_text: This Week’s Featured Headlines 1. Pennsylvania Invests $10M in Cybersecurity and $3.7M in Digital Permitting Modernization Source: Pennsylvania Office of Administration Newsroom | August 12, 2026 Governor Shapiro's 2026-27 budget adds $10 million in new cybersecurity funding and $3.7 million for digital permitting modernization through the Commonwealth Office of Digital Experience, which is part of a cybersecurity investment that has grown by $30 million over the past three years. ‍ What happened The $10 million cybersecurity investment builds on a multi-year strategy to strengthen monitoring across state networks and applications and improve real-time threat detection, with the cumulative three-year total signaling a sustained and growing commitment to cyber resilience that is actively producing procurement activity rather than still in planning stages. The $3.7 million for CODE PA will fund continued modernization of permitting processes in collaboration with the Department of Environmental Protection, building on existing digital tools including the PAyback money-back guarantee system and a permit tracking tool while expanding the state's track record of saving $37 million in IT spending through in-house modernization work. What it means for you Cybersecurity vendors offering network monitoring, threat detection, and endpoint protection should treat Pennsylvania as an active and repeat buyer, with $10 million flowing into a mature multi-year program that is procuring solutions rather than starting from scratch. Digital permitting platform vendors, environmental compliance technology firms, and government UX specialists should monitor procurement activity from CODE PA and DEP as the permitting modernization effort expands into new workflows and agency partnerships. 2. Massachusetts Provides $2M in Grants to Harden Water Utility Cybersecurity Source: Government Technology | August 12, 2026 The Massachusetts Clean Water Trust is providing at least $2 million in grant funding to help local water suppliers upgrade cybersecurity defenses, targeting small and disadvantaged communities whose aging infrastructure and limited budgets have left them most exposed to attack. ‍ What happened Grants of up to $50,000 are available to eligible public water suppliers for cybersecurity risk assessments and operational technology upgrades, with the program created in 2024 and already having distributed $1.3 million to 38 water systems, demonstrating active and ongoing deployment rather than a new initiative still finding its footing. State officials identified outdated software, weak network security, vulnerable access controls, and a lack of employee cybersecurity training as the primary threats to water infrastructure, pointing directly to the categories of solutions that funded water systems will be purchasing with grant money. What it means for you OT security vendors, cybersecurity assessment firms, and water utility technology providers should prioritize outreach to Massachusetts water suppliers, particularly smaller and rural systems that are newly eligible for funding and actively seeking implementation partners to help them spend grants efficiently before program deadlines. The explicit identification of weak access controls, unpatched software, and untrained staff as the primary vulnerabilities means vendors with solutions in identity management, patch management, and cybersecurity workforce training have particularly strong alignment with what funded systems will be buying. 3. Illinois Awards $50M to Rural Hospital Network for Technology Modernization and Workforce Development Source: PR Newswire | August 12, 2026 The Illinois Critical Access Hospital Network received more than $50 million from the Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services to administer rural health transformation grants to 60 small and rural hospitals serving approximately 1.4 million residents across the state. ‍ What happened The three grant agreements, signed July 31 and effective August 1, will fund technology modernization and infrastructure improvements at rural hospitals, chronic disease prevention programs, and workforce sustainability efforts including recruitment, training, and retention of healthcare professionals in underserved areas. ICAHN was selected as the largest sub-awardee of Illinois' $193 million first-year Rural Health Transformation Program allocation, giving it significant authority to direct funds to the 60 hospitals in its network, serving communities where 89 of 102 counties are designated Health Professional Shortage Areas with more than 3.5 million residents lacking adequate provider access. What it means for you Health IT vendors, electronic health records firms, and clinical technology providers should move quickly to engage ICAHN and its 60 member hospitals now that grant agreements are executed and funds are active, as technology modernization is one of three named funding priorities and recipients are under pressure to deploy funds before federal deadlines. The workforce sustainability initiative creates additional opportunities for healthcare staffing platforms, credentialing software, and rural recruitment technology firms, as Illinois hospitals are actively seeking tools to build long-term provider pipelines in communities where shortages are already severe. 4. Florida Awards $188M in Rural Health Grants to Organizations Serving 1.2 Million Residents Source: Florida Phoenix | August 11, 2026 The DeSantis administration announced $188 million in competitive grants to organizations across the state to improve healthcare access for 1.2 million rural Floridians, with technology-enabled care receiving the largest share of funding through a single awardee. ‍ What happened Community Health IT received approximately $44 million across four regional awards, the largest single recipient in this round, to support preventive care and care-at-home services across Northeast, Southwest, Southeast, and Northwest Florida, with the concentration of funding in one technology-forward organization signaling the state's deliberate prioritization of tech-enabled care delivery models. Florida's 31 rural counties were divided into four geographic regions for grant administration, with the Northwest Florida region receiving $81 million as the largest allocation, and grant categories spanning preventive and home-based care, value-based care, rural and satellite clinics, workforce initiatives, and health and lifestyle programs. What it means for you Telehealth vendors, remote patient monitoring firms, and care coordination platform providers should monitor procurement activity from Community Health IT and other large awardees as they stand up regional care-at-home programs across Florida's rural communities with funds they must deploy by September 2027. Florida's Year Two allocation will equal whatever the state actually spends by September 2027, creating strong financial incentive for all grantees to move quickly on implementation, meaning vendors who can demonstrate deployable solutions and fast onboarding timelines will have a meaningful advantage in winning contracts from organizations under spending pressure. 5. Nebraska Awards $136M in Rural Health Grants, Prioritizing Remote Patient Monitoring Technology Source: Nebraska Public Media | August 11, 2026 Nebraska has committed approximately $136 million of its $218.5 million first-year Rural Health Transformation Program allocation through nearly 200 grant agreements, with remote patient monitoring technology for 22 rural hospitals representing one of the largest and most explicitly tech-focused awards in the state's portfolio. ‍ What happened The Nebraska High Value Network, a partnership of 22 rural hospitals, received roughly $18 million to deploy remote patient monitoring technology including wearable BioButton devices that track respiration rates, blood pressure, and other patient health measurements from both hospital and home settings, combined with data system improvements that allow participating hospitals to aggregate monitoring data and evaluate its effectiveness in reducing emergency room visits and improving chronic disease management. Nebraska must award its remaining first-year funds to grantees by October 30, 2026 or risk losing the unspent balance to redistribution among other states, with DHHS officials confirming that currently available funding opportunities are forecast to cover Nebraska's full $218.5 million allocation, and a few grant opportunities remain open for eligible organizations to apply. What it means for you Remote patient monitoring vendors, wearable health device providers, and health data integration firms should treat Nebraska's High Value Network investment as a concrete near-term procurement opportunity, as 22 rural hospitals are now funded and actively building the infrastructure to deploy and evaluate these tools at scale across the state. With the October 30 obligation deadline approaching, vendors offering deployable solutions in Nebraska's funded categories including remote monitoring devices, health data integration platforms, VR-based EMS training systems, oral health platforms, and behavioral health tools should prioritize outreach now as remaining grant recipients finalize their implementation plans. title: We Taught folk to Shop in 10 Minutes
summary: How the AI that lives in your texts became the friend with good taste — powered by Channel3.
body_text: If you haven't met folk yet, it's a personal AI that lives right inside your iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram. You text it the way you'd text a friend — “book me a table,” “watch this flight,” “remind me to call my mum” — and it executes. Yesterday, Arlan, the founder of folk and a friend from our YC batch, texted to see if we could link up Channel3 with folk to help with all things shopping. In 10 minutes, folk connected to the Channel3 API, made its first search call, and started answering shopping queries — with structured product data, live prices, live stock, and a monetized buy link all powered up. Watch it work folk hunts down three clean, pre-owned, in-stock pairs and links straight to checkout: Ferragamo Vara bow pumps — $59.50, 30% offStuart Weitzman kitten pumps — $87.00, 40% off Pretty cool, right? What's actually happening Channel3 is the product data layer for AI-native shopping. As assistants like folk become a real place where people buy things, they need product data that's structured, always-fresh, and trustworthy — otherwise your AI confidently recommends a sold-out sweater in the wrong color, and everyone loses. So we give folk: Recommendations pulled from a universal catalog of real products Live prices and stock Price tracking Monetization, because every product folk surfaces is tracked through the retailer's affiliate program Why this is fun The whole point of folk is that it meets you where you already are. If you use folk to help book restaurants, and you want to use it to shop, you can. We'll be spotlighting more developers who are building awesome products on Channel3's API in the future — if you want to know more, check out our website: trychannel3.com .

title: Andy Burnham’s Social Care Reform Push: Families Reveal the True Cost of Caring for Loved Ones
